This course also explores the implications for what the law should be.  The economic approach to law places emphasis on the criterion of efficiency, particularly in analyzing private law (property, contract and tort law).  The course also addresses criticisms of the economic approach to law, in particular, the redistributive approach to private law.

Economic analysis of law is considered from a number of the following perspectives: the Chicago School (Neoclassical Law and Economics); Public Choice theory; New Institutional Law and Economics; and Behavioral Law and Economics.  Economic analysis is applied to some of the following areas of law: property law (including the law of intellectual property); contract law; tort law; corporate law; competition law and consumer protection law; criminal law; and litigation process and alternative dispute resolution.

By the end of the course, students should be able to use microeconomic analysis to address a variety of topics in the law.  Illustrative topics are the ownership of genetic material, enforceability of shrink-wrap licenses, products liability, attorney-client privilege, and the duty to report a crime, to name but a few.  The economic approach to law even lends itself to analyzing such an arcane topic as property interests in sunken treasure.

name: Revenue Law

school.name: Yong Pung How School of Law

description: This course seeks to instill knowledge and appreciation of the main principles of tax law in Singapore . As tax is a creature of statute, an understanding of the promulgation and interpretation of statutory provisions is included in the course. The course covers income tax, which forms the bulk of the course topics, property tax, goods and services tax, stamp duties and estate duty. Students will study how tax legislation is applied by the Singapore courts to both corporate and individual taxpayers on specific tax issues, and will be exposed to a variety of case authorities emanating from several jurisdictions with tax laws similar to our own. Having become acquainted with fundamental tax concepts and principles, students are led into the analysis of the decided cases relating to topics in the course. These topics include the taxation of business income of companies and employment income of individuals. In addition to tax issues on income sourced in Singapore , the course devotes a seminar to international taxation, which also touches on tax issues in electronic commerce. For a balanced approach to the study of revenue law, as a complement to the treatment of substantive tax issues, the method and manner of dealing with tax assessments, objections and appeals under our tax system are also dwelt upon. This endeavours to make students familiar with the processes involved in, and procedural aspects of, the resolution of tax disputes. This tax course also seeks to deliver a practical approach on how tax issues arise and are handled in real life, to equip and prepare students for the world of business after completion of their studies.

name: Banking Law

school.name: Yong Pung How School of Law

description: Banking Law

name: Risk and Reg in Real Estate
longName: Risk and Regulations in Real Estate

school.name: Yong Pung How School of Law

description:
This course focuses on the legal fundamentals of real estate practice and development in Singapore. While space and the built environment is ubiquitous, real estate remains a unique asset class. The rules relating to its current and future value, how it may be securely transferred from one party to another and its very definition all depend on law. The course is vital for students with an interest in real estate transactions, its development, investment and financing.

The primary topics covered include the nature of real property, contract and property torts, interests in property, development and construction, the rules relating to securitisation and taxes affecting property. It is one of the foundational courses of the Real Estate Track offered in LKCSB and SOE in Singapore Management University.
tracks: PLE: Public Policy and Governance Track

name: Credit & Security Law

school.name: Yong Pung How School of Law

description: This course aims to provide a basic understanding of the legal aspects of obtaining funds for a business through debt financing, with a particular focus on secured debt financing. As such, it considers the legal issues involved in various forms of extending credit, such as loans, credit cards and hire-purchase. It will also examine the types of assets that may be given as security to raise funds, and the various forms of security interests such as mortgages, charges and guarantees.  The legal issues pertaining to each form of security will be explored.  The course concludes with a consideration of the liabilities of a business and, correspondingly, a creditor’s remedies and priority position in the event of default in repayment.

name: Consumer & Marketing Law

school.name: Yong Pung How School of Law

description: The objective of the course is to equip students with the knowledge of Consumer and Marketing Law. The course would cover the law relating to the sale and supply of goods and services in Singapore including, among other things, the law of sales, hire-purchase, consumer credit, product liability and e-commerce. Further the course will deal with the law relating to advertising and marketing devises such as multi-level marketing, licensing and franchising. The course will then consider methods of consumer protection including the Consumer Protection (Fair Trading) Act and the roles of agencies such as CASE and the Small Claims Tribunal.

name: Law of Generational Wealth Pln

school.name: Yong Pung How School of Law

description:
This course lays the foundation of knowing the laws that facilitate wealth planning and management. In planning for self as well as the “next generation’, a person has to consider not only preserving, but also growth of, capital; short term as well as long term investments; and how to segregate business wealth from private wealth.  As the size of the wealthbase grows, the scope of wealth planning will go beyond national borders.

This course will build upon the knowledge of the basic business law course, especially contract and tort, and will add to a student’s knowledge by the inclusion of tax law and other generation planning related laws.  This course has an international flavour to it as students will be exposed to basic comparison of the laws of at least two countries.  Furthermore, the emphasis of this course is not on the principles only, but on the application of such laws to wealth planning and management.

name: Law of Confi Info, TS & Pvcy
longName: Law of Confidential Information, Trade Secrets & Privacy

school.name: Yong Pung How School of Law

description:
It is a truism that the world at large and Singapore in particular has entered the information age where knowledge and new ideas will form the bedrock of the new economic order. This course has the aim of setting out a thorough overview of the rationale and principles governing  protection of confidential information outside of the statutory intellectual and industrial property rights. The course will also examine a number of areas of current special concern. These include: industrial (commercial) espionage and the balance of rights and obligations of confidentiality as between an employer and employee. Both of these are likely to be of increasing importance in Singapore and the international market place in years to come. The course also has the objective of deepening appreciation of how the common law system works and the overlaps that can arise between different pigeon holes within the law of obligations. By examining the rationale for protection as well as different legal theories by which confidential information can be protected, students should at the end of the course acquire a better awareness of the workings of contract, tort and property law principles. 

Aside from industrial (commercial) confidential information, the course will explore the interface between privacy and confidentiality. In a world where information is a premium and information technology ubiquitous, “informational privacy” or “informational self-autonomy” is likely to become as important as reputational interests and bodily self-autonomy.  This is well illustrated by the recent litigation by Naomi Campbell, Michael Douglas and Catherine Zeta Jones. Discussion of the rapidly developing law in the area will be intellectually challenging and highly topical for Singapore and the international market because of its international importance. The question of protecting informational privacy is more than a matter of personal concern to individuals: adequate safeguards may become increasingly important in the data processing industry.

name: US Constitutional Law & Hist

school.name: Yong Pung How School of Law

description: The course examines the process behind the creation of a new nation from a loose confederation of thirteen distinctly different British colonies.  That new nation has gone through a series of “revolutions” that have many of their roots in issues that were apparent even at the time of the original revolution against British rule in the 1770s.  Slavery was the most difficult issue, and the disputes over slavery led to a terrible Civil War in 1861-65.  The nation was re-formed after the Civil War, but almost collapsed again during the Great Depression that began with the stock market crashes of 1929.  The result of government intervention in the economy was the creation of a new concept of the central government as fundamental as that which occurred after 1865.  In the 1950s and 1960s the Civil Rights Movement was a peaceful revolution that ended the last legal vestiges of slavery.  The Constitution has been the fundamental framework and point of reference for all dramatic national changes.  It remains so today, and it also is the matrix for determining the scope of personal, individual rights.  Study of the history of the Constitution, the governing document of the oldest democratic republic in continuous existence, provides an opportunity to analyze and to understand the role of law in creating and maintaining a stable, but flexible, framework for the ordering of a heterogeneous society.

name: Cont Nego, Draft & Interpret

school.name: Yong Pung How School of Law

description: This course deals with the law and practice relating to the negotiation, drafting and interpretation of contracts. It begins by looking at the theory and practice of negotiation. It then considers the evidentiary problems of different ways of making contracts, ranging from contracts which are wholly oral to those which are wholly written and signed. Next, the course focuses on how contracts and contract terms are construed and interpreted. Finally, the principles learnt are put into practice through examining standard form contracts and other documents.

name: Law of Mergers & Acquisitions

school.name: Yong Pung How School of Law

description:
Mergers and acquisitions raise legal issues that will affect strategy, deal structure, legal responsibilities and liabilities. An understanding and sensitivity to such issues will be valuable for future business leaders, investment bankers, business consultants and entrepreneurs and will enhance their effectiveness. 
This course examines mergers and acquisitions transactions from the transactional perspective. The topics that would be covered include mechanics of structuring mergers and acquisitions transactions, the preparatory work that is required in connection therewith, the regulatory environment in which mergers and acquisitions take place, duties of participants engaged in mergers and acquisitions (including financial advisers and directors of acquirors and target companies), deal protections, deal tactics for friendly and hostile bids, disclosure obligations, compulsory acquisitions and financing. 
The course aims to provide an understanding of the legal regime under which mergers and acquisitions are regulated in Singapore and the focus is on the acquisition of publicly listed companies. Comparisons with jurisdictions such as United States, Australia, United Kingdom and Hong Kong will be made. 
Case studies, adapted from real life examples, will be used extensively in the course.

name: Law, Life Sci & Gene Engrg
longName: Law, Life Sciences and Genetic Engineering

school.name: Yong Pung How School of Law

description:
Alongside information technology, biotechnology and the life sciences has been identified as one of the major engines to power Singapore’s industrial and economic growth in her next phase of economic development. Indeed, the life science industry is already highly competitive in the international market place. Established players include, the United States, the European Union (especially the United Kingdom) and Japan. Significant new entrants include: China, India, Malaysia, South Korea and of course Singapore.

This course seeks to provide students with an overview of the interface between life sciences, biotechnology and the law. The course will commence with lectures and discussions of the science behind the modern biotechnology revolution. This will set the scene for a teasing out of some of the main areas where legal issues have arisen of late.  What then follows is a discussion in more detail of some specific areas. Whilst the selection of specific areas will vary from year to year, the main areas are likely to be incentive aspects (the need for appropriate intellectual and industrial property rights); public health aspects (access to medicines and the impact of modern patent laws); third world development and environmental aspects (biodiversity and biopiracy issues especially in relation to the interface between TRIPs and the Convention on Biodiversty) and the rights of individuals and genetic information (genetic privacy, genetic research and related matters).

name: Negotiation

school.name: Yong Pung How School of Law

description:
Negotiation introduces students to fundamental concepts in interest-based negotiation. The 7 elements of interest-based negotiation will provide the participants with a framework for a more structured approach towards preparing for and handling negotiation.

Students will also learn various communication and relationship building strategies. A number of these concepts are from the field of neuro-linguistic programming. The application of such concepts is new and represents one of the latest advances in the field of negotiation.

In addition, students will be provided with a dynamic communication framework for the analysis of negotiations. The focus will be on why some conversations seem to be fraught with difficulty and how a negotiator can have more productive conversations during and even after negotiations.

Fluency in English, both written and spoken is necessary and may impact assessment.

Attendance at ALL classes is crucial and will impact assessment, in particular the 1st two classes as these are foundational classes. Please note that unconfirmed students will NOT be allowed to attend the class.

name: Conflict Resolution

school.name: Yong Pung How School of Law

description:
Conflict Resolution introduces students to fundamental concepts in interest-based conflict management. The 7 elements of interest-based conflict management will provide the participants with a framework for a more structured approach towards preparing for and handling conflict.

Students will also learn the various stages of a mediation session based on the model endorsed by the SMC. There will be discussions about what each stage seeks to achieve and illustrations on how to work towards the goals.

In addition, students will be introduced to various key communication skills which form the basic skills-set required for conflict management. They will learn that effective communications is critical to conflict management. They will also be given practical strategies that they can use to overcome different types of impasse that they are likely to encounter while mediating.

Fluency in English, both written and spoken is necessary and may impact assessment.

Attendance at ALL classes is crucial and will impact assessment, in particular the 1st two classes as these are foundational classes. Please note that unconfirmed students will NOT be allowed to attend the class.

name: Negotiat'n & Conflict Resol.

school.name: Yong Pung How School of Law

description:
Negotiation & Conflict Resolution introduces students to fundamental concepts in interest-based negotiation and conflict resolution. The 7 elements of interest-based negotiation and conflict resolution will provide the participants with a framework for a more structured approach towards preparing for and handling negotiation and conflict resolution.

Students will also learn various communication and relationship building strategies. A number of these concepts are from the field of neuro-linguistic programming. The application of such concepts is new and represents one of the latest advances in the field of negotiation.  In addition, students will be provided with a dynamic communication framework for the analysis of negotiations. The focus will be on why some conversations seem to be fraught with difficulty and how a negotiator can have more productive conversations during and even after negotiations.

Students will learn the various stages of a mediation session based on the model endorsed by the SMC. There will be discussions about what each stage seeks to achieve and illustrations on how to work towards the goals.  In addition, students will be introduced to various key communication skills which form the basic skills-set required for conflict management. They will learn that effective communications is critical to conflict management. They will also be given practical strategies that they can use to overcome different types of impasse that they are likely to encounter while mediating.

Fluency in English, both written and spoken is necessary and may impact assessment.

Attendance at ALL classes is crucial and will impact assessment, in particular the 1st two classes as these are foundational classes. Please note that unconfirmed students will NOT be allowed to attend the class.

name: Law of International Trade

school.name: Yong Pung How School of Law

description:
The results of sale transactions are all around us. Most goods – such as the chair you may be sitting on, the computer from which you may be reading this, and the food you may have recently eaten - have reached consumers and business organizations as a result of sales. The buying and selling of goods is a fundamental aspect of domestic and international business, and Singapore is a well-known centre of trade, as a consumer of both local and foreign goods. Given that sale transactions are a common part of daily life, a sound understanding of the law regulating sales is important for an entrepreneur and for the management of resources in organizations.

This course will provide an overview of the rules that apply to sale transactions, an understanding of major differences between domestic and international sales, common trade terms, and major methods of financing sales and of transporting goods across borders. It will also provide an understanding of the wider national and international environments in which international trade takes place, including product liability laws, major methods of resolving trade disputes, and important regulatory issues, such as WTO rules, and laws on customs, competition, technology transfer and security.
tracks: Ops Mgmt Major: Maritime Business & Ops Track

name: Trade and Business Dispute Res

school.name: Yong Pung How School of Law

description: This elective will introduce students to common sources of business disputes including contract, intellectual property, product liability and regulatory disputes. It will then examine the various forms of methods used to settle such business disputes especially in a cross-border context, as well as dispute avoidance techniques. It will cover the advantages and disadvantages of negotiations, mediation, arbitration, litigation and trade actions available to private business operators, relevance of regional arbitration bodies, ASEAN and other regional trade arrangements, and how business disputes that escalate to State level are resolved at the World Trade Organization and other external fora. The course will be taught interactively through seminars, role-play scenarios and group discussions.

name: Chinese Business Law

school.name: Yong Pung How School of Law

description: The People’s Republic of China (PRC) is the world’s largest potential marketplace. International investors can expect enormous business and investment opportunities. To meet the need for up-to-date legal information, this course will provide students with a brief introduction to the legal framework for doing business in China. The main emphasis will be on the areas of contract law, company law, foreign investment law and land law. The course will focus on the current practical legal issues related to the above mentioned areas.

name: Chinese Hist, Cul, Econ & Law
longName: Introduction to Chinese History, Culture, Economy and Law (Mandarin)

school.name: Yong Pung How School of Law

description:
China’s rapid economic development in the last 30 years has attracted increasing global attention. More than ever before, foreign businesses and businessmen are heading to China to do business or to work. Often, these businessmen encounter culture shock and other problems even though they are able to speak Chinese. This is because of inadequate preparation before going to China. They are often handicapped by their limited knowledge and understanding of China. This course is therefore designed to meet this need. It is aimed at helping to produce bilingual and bicultural professionals who will be better equipped to do business in China. This course will therefore be conducted in Mandarin, and introduce students to important aspects of modern China: its rich and long history; traditional culture, complicated economic development and unique legal system. In the short term, it will help students going to China for internship or Study Missions to enhance their language skills and acquire a general background understanding of modern China. In the long run, it will stand them in good stead in the future when they do business with or work in China.

This course will be conducted in Mandarin. Students should be able to understand, read and write Mandarin. Basically, students who have passed their GCE O-level Chinese examination should be qualified to take this course. Students who come from China and have received education above high school level in China are not eligible to take this course.

name: WTO: Law, Economics & Policy
longName: World Trade Organization: Law, Economics and Policy

school.name: Yong Pung How School of Law

description:
Since its establishment in 1994, the World Trade Organization (WTO) has become the most important international organization for business firms across the globe. Its ever expansive rules now cover issues ranging from trade in both industrial and agricultural products, trade in services, labor mobility, investment, free trade agreements, and a wide variety of domestic regulatory regimes. What are these rules? How are these rules made? What are the economic rationales for these rules? What are the impacts of these rules on both international and domestic firms? How can firms use these rules to protect and advance their interests? This course, taught by a former lawyer at the WTO Secretariat, will provide students with an opportunity to examine these issues with a critical perspective.

For those who want to work for international firms, this course is important because it can help you to learn some of the most important international rules governing trade and investment worldwide. Even for those who want to work for Singapore-based firms, this course is important because WTO rules affect many businesses in Singapore, the country with the highest trade to GDP ratio in the world.

name: Chinese Foreign Investment Law

school.name: Yong Pung How School of Law

description: This course is aimed at students who wish to do business or involving in foreign direct investment (FDI) in China. The module will introduce students to the main FDI forms and especially the laws and the relevant legislations governing these forms, e.g. equity joint ventures, contractual joint ventures, wholly foreign--owned enterprises, limited liability companies and the Merger & Acquisition in China. It will provide students with a critical understanding of the FDI regime as well as the relationship between the FDI governing laws and other general laws so that they will be able to get accurate information and updated legal advice in this area.

name: Intr to Ind Democracy: S L & R
longName: Introduction to Indian Democracy: State, Law & Rights

school.name: Yong Pung How School of Law

description: This course is about India’s democracy. Born in 1947, India – both as an idea and as a polity – is uniquely complex and contradictory. With nearly 1.2 billion people, at least 22 official languages, all major religions and hundreds of caste and sub-caste groups, it is a political and social experiment unparalleled in world history.  Understanding India, in large measure, is about understanding the processes of continuity and change – of tradition and modernity – through which she experiences herself. With that objective in mind, this course will introduce students to some of the key debates and conflicts that have shaped modern India.

name: Intl Law & Global Politics

school.name: Yong Pung How School of Law

description: This course will introduce international law theory and practices that concern contemporary global issues, which range from the Palestinian Authority’s United Nations statehood bid, South China Sea disputes to the economic crisis in Europe.  The course is not only designed for students seeking to acquire basic knowledge necessary to pursue a career related to international relations or transnational business, but also for students who wish to understand the in-depth legal and political analysis of real-world situations.  Each class will begin with an introduction to international law principles, followed by case study discussions. The course will cover legal issues such as custom and treaties under international law, the relation between international and domestic law, the determination of statehood and recognition policy, national governments’ jurisdiction and immunity, states’ international responsibility, the role of international courts, and the legal structures of international organizations.  Due to the fast-growing development in international issues in Asia, the course will also focus on practices of Singapore, China, and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN).

name: Entertainment Law

school.name: Yong Pung How School of Law

description: This course will examine the legal and regulatory issues relating (and of concern) to the media and entertainment industry. These issues will straddle various media platforms such as print, music, film and the Internet. The areas of law that will be covered include: Contracts and licensing issues; the role of statutory bodies (i.e. MICA, MDA and IDA) and content regulation (free speech and censorship); relevant torts like defamation, the law of confidence and privacy as well as copyright and trademark issues (including rights clearances and the role of IPOS). The focus will be on the Singapore law and regulatory regime although references will be made, where relevant or necessary, to developments in foreign jurisdictions, particularly US and UK law.

name: Health Law and Medical Ethics

school.name: Yong Pung How School of Law

description: This course covers issues relating to health/medical law such as medical negligence, consent to treatment, confidentiality, and the Mental Capacity Act.  It will also explore ethical theories pertinent to the practice of medicine and the Singapore Medical Council’s Ethical Code and Ethical Guidelines 2016, as well as certain legal and ethical issues relating to reproduction and end-of-life.
tracks: PLE: Public Policy and Governance Track

name: The Legal Env of Business
longName: The Legal Environment of Business: An Asian Perspective

school.name: Yong Pung How School of Law

description:
Law does not exist in a vacuum, and neither do businesses –law provides the backbone upon which businesses operate. Armed with some basic knowledge, entrepreneurs should be able to better structure their businesses, avoid common legal pitfalls, and identify potential problems, and take appropriate actions, both before and after the problems arise. A failure to understand –at least rudimentarily –the impact of the legal landscape and certain legal developments on business transactions often has dire consequences.

This is an introductory course designed to help acquaint students –who may be future business owners or managers –with the legal environment within which businesses operate and the common legal issues one may face when doing business in Asia, with a particular emphasis on Singapore. The course will entail not only classroom teaching and learning, but will also include invaluable sharing sessions guest speakers from various relevant fields, as well as field trips to legal institutions and/or offices in Singapore.

A substantial part of the course will be dedicated to exploring, at a general level, various aspects of laws pertaining to doing business, with an especial focus on business organisations and commercial transactions.

With cross-border business dealings being the norm instead of the exception, an understanding of the implications of contractual clauses in international contracts, and of the avenues for the resolution of international disputes, also become essential.

Because business relationships with commercial parties are primarily governed by contract, an understanding of how contracts work is important. Basic principles of contract law (e.g. the making and performance of contracts), as well as laws applying to specific situations (e.g. the sale of goods and services), will be taught in brief. Students will also be introduced to the law of torts and will, in particular, learn the essentials of the very pervasive tort of negligence, and the often-misunderstood tort of defamation.

name: China's BRI: Challenges & Opp
longName: China's Belt and Road Initiative: Challenges and Opportunities

school.name: Yong Pung How School of Law

description:
Initially two obscure projects (The Silk Road Economic Belt and the 21st-century Maritime Silk Road) announced in 2013, the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) has quickly become the centre-piece of China’s economic diplomacy over the past few years. Spanning across Asia, Europe and Africa, the project is often called the “Marshall Plan” of China as it aims to promote the economic development of the
less-developed countries in the three continents.

Taught by an advisor to the WTO and the Chinese government, this course will provide an in-depth analysis for the background for the BRI, the detailed strategy of China in each areas covered such as trade and investment, and how the BRI might result in an alternative economic order led by China.

name: Financial Crime

school.name: Yong Pung How School of Law

description:
This course will introduce students to key issues in domestic and international financial crime. It begins with the basic principles of criminal law in Singapore. Students will also learn how evidence is obtained in the course of investigations and how that evidence may be used to charge and convict offenders in court. The course will then progress to cover the major types of financial crime, such as: (1) cheating, criminal breach of trust and criminal misappropriation of property; (2) corruption; (3) market misconduct: insider trading and market manipulation; (4) tax evasion; and (5) money laundering and terrorist financing. Efforts to combat international financial crime, e.g. the setting up of the Financial Action Task Force, anti-money laundering procedures, and mutual legal assistance and exchange of information regimes, will also be discussed in this course.

This course will be taught with its main audience in mind, namely, students taking a second major in Financial Forensics offered by the School of Accountancy.

name: Sus, MNC and Intl Law
longName: Sustainability, Multinational Corporations and International Law

school.name: Yong Pung How School of Law

description:
Sustainable development has become a key concept for the 21st century and has been endorsed and recognised in a number of instruments of international law. Problems like global climate change, high pollution levels and depletion of living and non-living natural resources are becoming important restraints on the global economy. These sustainability challenges will reshape the global economy. The transition to a greener, more sustainable economic system will require collective action by governments, international organizations, multinational corporations, and civil society.  

This course reviews the principles and rules underlying the post-war international economic order, in particular with respect to trade, foreign investment and finance, as well as some of its key institutions, such as the World Bank and the World Trade Organization. The course reviews the role of international economic agreements in pursuing sustainable development.

name: Prof. Ethics & CFA Ethics
description: Participants will develop an appreciation and understanding of business, financial and professional ethics. This course explores responsibility from competing theoretical and management perspectives. It will also analyze conflict situations in the various personal, corporate and professional settings, and how to avoid and manage these conflicts. Topics includes prudent financial management, product safety, corporate responsibility and the implementation of CFA ethical standards.

name: Financial Advisers Law
description: The course will cover the law of contract and essential aspects of partnership and company law important for wealth management. Topics will include the legal framework for the supervision of financial institutions, industry norms, standards of practice, and self-regulatory rules applicable to asset management and personal financial advice. It will cover relevant aspects of tort.

name: Legal Environment of Business
description: This course is designed to help business students acquaint themselves with the framework of Singapore's legal system and to understand the legal environment within which businesses operate. A substantial part of the course is dedicated to the study of contractual principles as the making and performance of contracts form the rudiment of all businesses. In addition, this course will also cover the main body of laws that regulate the operational aspects of companies embodied in the Companies Act.

name: Int, Resp & Good Govern in Bus
longName: Integrity, Responsibility and Good Governance in Business
description:
Ethical and socially responsible conduct and good governance are treated with increasing importance and prominence by the corporate world, governments, the public, civil society, and other stakeholders globally. The integrity, reputation and success of organizations and individuals are increasingly and intricately linked with the level of ethical conduct, social responsibility and accountability to a varied range of stakeholders.

It is also increasingly evident that society and governments expect the business world to behave ethically and be socially responsible, with self-regulation and norm-generation being favoured approaches in dealing with the impact of business on various aspects of our lives.

This course aims to sensitize participants to the issues and concerns of business ethics and social responsibility. It seeks to equip participants with the conceptual tools and thinking/ethical processes by which decisions are made and evaluated when businesses/individuals are confronted with ethical and moral dilemmas. It is also hoped that a good understanding of ethics can be applied to the development of frameworks and environments that promote good governance.

Although this is an academic course with real world relevance, it is certainly neither intended to make ‘saints’ out of ‘sinners’, or to propose the merits of a virtuous life. Instead, what it aspires towards is to engage, inform, and sensitize participants in critically evaluating the trends, societal concerns and expectations while encouraging participants to develop a personal perspective about ethics, integrity, personal and corporate responsibility—informed by rigorous and nuanced understanding of the knowledge and theoretical approaches—in business and professional life.

name: Fin Advisers Law & Compliance
description:
This course aims to give participants a good appreciation of the law as it affects providing financial advice, marketing of financial products and compliance. 

The first part of the course assists participants to understand the law. It will address the regulatory framework imposed by statute and relevant authorities, including the Financial Advisers Act, MAS Notices, Guidelines and other publications. It also discusses tort, contract law, negligence, fiduciary duties of client advisers and consumer rights. It also addresses misrepresentation and non-reliance clauses. Participants will also be introduced to agency law, conflict of laws and the interplay between the regulatory law, tort law and contract law. 

The second part of this course will also provide an ethical and practical approach to compliance and risk in view of heightened regulatory requirements that impact wealth managers. Regulatory framework and regulations such as Anti Money Laundering, Fair Dealing and Tax Oﬀences will be introduced to discuss issues relevant to the wealth management industry, and strategy for Singapore as a wealth centre, private banks and trust companies, and for individuals seeking to make a career in the industry. In addition, different types of risks that can impact the wealth management business, and how such risks can be managed with renewed rigour in areas such as client suitability, enhanced due diligence in client onboarding will be addressed.

name: Corporate Governance & Ethics
description:
Ethical and socially responsible conduct and corporate governance are treated with increasing importance and prominence by the corporate world, governments, the public, and other stakeholders globally. The reputation and success of organizations (and individuals associated with them) are increasingly and intricately linked with the level of ethical conduct, social responsibility and accountability to a varied range of stakeholders. 

It is also increasingly evident that society and governments expect the business world to behave ethically and be socially responsible, with self-regulation and norm-generation being favoured approaches in dealing with the impact of business on various aspects of our lives. 

This course aims to sensitise participants to the issues and concerns of business ethics and social responsibility, and to a lesser extent, corporate governance. It seeks to equip participants with the conceptual tools and thinking/ethical processes by which decisions are made and evaluated when businesses/individuals are confronted with ethical and moral dilemmas. Corporate governance is enhanced if it moves away from a compliance mindset to one where a business entity conducts its business activities in an enlightened manner. 

Although this is an academic course with real world relevance, it is certainly not intended to make ‘saints’ out of ‘sinners’ or to propose the merits of a virtuous life. What it aspires towards is to engage and sensitise participants in critically evaluating the trends, societal concerns and expectations while encouraging participants to develop a personal perspective about ethics—informed by rigorous and nuanced understanding of the knowledge and theoretical approaches—in business and professional life.

name: Bus Sust, Intel Prop & Val Ext
longName: Business Sustainability, Intellectual Property and Value Extraction
description:
This course addresses the issues of intellectual property (IP) in the pursuit of capturing value. The general order of topics is: 1+2. Introduction to Intellectual Property (IP) Rights I and II; 3. How Firms Can Use IP To Extract Value: Case Study Analyses and Presentations; 4. Legal Perspective I: Different Types of IP-Related Contracts; 5. Legal Perspective II: IP Due Diligence in Corporate Transaction; 6. IP – Value Extraction: An R&D Perspective; 7. IP – Value Extraction: Examples of Value Extraction through Technological Innovation and Commercialisation; 8. Legal Perspective III: IP Management and Litigation. This course will examine the different ways in which value may be extracted from the ownership of intellectual property rights (IPRs) and provide an understanding of the threats and opportunities that IPRs provide to all businesses.

The course will start with a general introduction into intellectual property rights (IPR’s) which are important when considering the development of an effective IP management and valuation cum extraction strategy. We will also look at the legal underpinnings and the proper management of IP rights (IPRs) in the context of their commercialisation. The course will look at ways of exploiting different IPRs and the different challenges they present. We will consider how to and why it is necessary to conduct IP due diligence in corporate transactions, and participants will be taken through some practical steps that should be employed to undertake this effectively. Further, this course will show how technological and business innovations enable creation of sustainable wealth & value and outline strategies for extracting them. In continuation, it will examine practical examples of innovations to understand how they can create remarkable value. Importantly, we will consider the critical role IPRs play in extracting enterprise value. 

Based on various case studies, participants will be guided through the processes, tools and standards through which enterprises can engage in innovation, effective IPR management, commercialisation and, ultimately, value extraction.

The goal of this course is to introduce you to the real, practical considerations and opportunities involved in the management, commercialisation and effective exploitation of IPRs so that you are better able to deal with the issues as they arise and better recognise and manage these when they do.

name: Legal Issue & Risk in Business
longName: Legal Issues and Risks in Business
description: Just as the business world is very complex, the laws affecting business are also very complex. Yet it is critical for the CFO (and other members of senior management) of a corporation to have a good understanding, and some level of mastery, of the key legal issues and risks in business. This will help the corporation to optimise its rights and minimize its liabilities, and thereby enhance the corporation’s financial position. The field of law is very wide. In this course, we focus on the fundamentals and the critical concepts and problems. The topics covered are: introduction to law (including business model protection), negligence liability, contract law, corporate law (including agency law) and international aspects.

name: Financial Advisors and the Law
description:
This course aims to give participants a good appreciation of the law as it affects giving financial advice and selling financial products. It provides an overview of the subject and focuses on the key legal principles, the pertinent issues and problems and the measures that may be adopted. 

A vital part of this regime is the regulatory framework imposed by statute and by the relevant authority (in Singapore, the Monetary Authority of Singapore [MAS]). The labyrinth of regulation formed by the statutes (primarily the Financial Advisers Act), the subsidiary legislation (in particular the Financial Advisers Regulations) and the MAS Notices, Guidelines and other publications) is a comprehensive and complex framework which financial advisers  must understand, comply with and leverage upon. The course aims to give participants a good snapshot of this framework.

The counterpart to the regulatory regime is the civil liability regime, which has two main parts: tort law (primarily the tort of negligence) and contract law. As regards negligence, participants in the financial advice industry have rights and liabilities towards each other. The law of negligence is vast; in this course, we take a summary look at the tort of negligence and consider its application to financial advisory activity. 

As regards contract law, the course gives a quick overview of contract law and focuses on some of the more important issues and concepts pertinent to financial advisory work, such as misrepresentation and non-reliance clauses. 

In addition to tort law and contract law, participants will be briefly introduced to  fiduciary duty and international legal aspects. 

Participants are encouraged to ask freely any questions about the law in general or financial advisers law in particular.

name: Legal Issue & Risk in Business
longName: Legal Issues and Risks in Business
description: Just as the business world is very complex, the laws affecting business are also very complex. Yet it is critical for the CFO (and other members of senior management) of a corporation to have a good understanding, and some level of mastery, of the key legal issues and risks in business. This will help the corporation to optimise its rights and minimize its liabilities, and thereby enhance the corporation’s financial position. The field of law is very wide. In this course, we focus on the fundamentals and the critical concepts and problems. The topics covered are: introduction to law, negligence liability, contract law, law relating to intermediaries (or agency law), corporate law and international aspects.

name: Intel. Property, Data & Innov.
description:
This course is an introduction to intellectual property rights (IPRs), and their relationship to the knowledge economy. In a world where everything from songs to seeds, and colours to shapes, can be protected (and copied), a basic understanding of IPRs is essential. This course examines the various categories of rights, and the different threats and opportunities that they present for businesses. It also considers the extent to which IPRs can foster or hinder creativity and innovation.

During this course, we will differentiate the types of IPRs (such as patent, copyright, and trademark), and understand their strategic value in a commercial context. We will demystify basic terminology and debunk the key misconceptions and myths that exist. We will also explore diverse conceptual frameworks and approaches to thinking about ownership vs. licensing, proprietary vs. open source, and offense vs. defense. It is often said that IPRs can be both sword and shield: we will consider practical examples that demonstrate this duality, as well as the related tactical considerations for start-ups as well as established enterprises. 

The goal of this course is to introduce you to core concepts and practical considerations involved in the creation and management of IPRs, so that you are better able to deal with potential issues as they arise. It should help you ask important questions and weigh in on IP policies and approaches at your workplace.

name: Sustainability Law
description: We live in a hyperconnected world – ecosystems and societies are linked like never before. This occurs through the movement of people, goods and products and the transfer of capital and information. At the same time, there is mounting appreciation of the need to address issues of equity and sustainability concurrently. To adequately understand, and ultimately to govern and regulate, for equitable-sustainability there is the need to identify and appreciate the complex feedbacks across activities of multiple individual, government and corporate actors across scales from the global to the local. This interdisciplinary course equips students with a grounding in concepts from the biophysical sciences, social sciences, law and governance. It focuses on key social, ecological and economic concerns in the context of biodiversity and climate change. By introducing students to systems and futures approaches it enables students to engage in sustainable and equitable governance for more desirable tomorrows.
graduateOutcomes: Understanding of global and Asian perspectives

name: Legal Knowledge & Strategy for
longName: Legal Knowledge & Strategy for Senior Management
description: Just as the business world is very complex, the laws affecting business are also very complex. Yet, it is necessary for the senior management of a corporation to have a good understanding, and in fact some level of mastery, of the law in order that they may not just comply with but also leverage the law to their advantage. The field of law is very wide. In this course, we focus on the fundamentals and the critical concepts and problems. The topics covered are: introduction to law, corporate law, transactional law, negligence liability, law relating to intermediaries and international aspects.

name: Legal Knowledge & Strat for SM
longName: Legal Knowledge & Strategy for Senior Management
description: Just as the business world is very complex, the laws affecting business are also very complex. Yet, it is necessary for the senior management of a corporation to have a good understanding, and in fact some level of mastery, of the law in order that they may not just comply with but also leverage the law to their advantage. The field of law is very wide. In this course, we focus on the fundamentals and the critical concepts and problems. The topics covered are: introduction to law, corporate law, transactional law, negligence liability, law relating to intermediaries and international aspects.

name: Linguistics
description: Linguistics is the study of language in all its aspects. The purpose of this course is to acquaint students with some general principles of human language based on the fact that our capacity for language sets us apart from other species. The course will describe the structure of human languages (the heart of Linguistics), their history and the ways in which they evolve. The course will also cover the major branches of the discipline including phonetics and phonology, syntax, morphology, semantics, pragmatics and students will be introduced to the principles of applied linguistics such as sociolinguistics, psycholinguistics, neurolinguistics and second language acquisition.

name: Comm in China: Comp. & Strat
longName: Communication in China: Competencies and Strategies

school.name: Lee Kong Chian School of Business

description: This course, using Chinese as the instruction medium in class , will expose students to the general environment of China . It aims to enable students to gain a basic understanding of the guoqing or national conditions, society and people in China today. Ultimately it seeks to help students expand their communication skills repertoire and gain a competitive advantage for effective interpersonal communication for that particular context. The instructional methods for this course include lectures, case studies, and group-based learning projects and presentation. Guest speakers will be invited to share with the class their first-hand experience and observation from their business activities in China . Course evaluation will be based on students' participation in and contribution to class discussion and other learning activities.

name: Calculus
description: This course introduces to management and business students the basic concepts of calculus : functions, derivative and integration. The purpose of the course is to increase the students' confidence in their ability to solve business, economic and scientifc problems.

name: Corporate Entre. & Innovation

school.name: Lee Kong Chian School of Business

description: Large, established corporations face fundamentally different innovation challenges than new or young small firms. The routinization of practices, obsolescence of such routines and dominant logic that may be misaligned with changes in the environment subject large firms to great difficulties in innovating. Further, revenue cannibalization with existing products and the politics of allocating scarce resources away from established, competing product divisions afflict how new ventures are created within large corporations.  These issues have few parallels in new, small firms.  In view of typically bureaucratic hierarchies in large corporations, it is important for students to understand how to design and manage innovation systems for large corporations, as well as how to lead corporate entrepreneurship.

name: International Business

school.name: Lee Kong Chian School of Business

description: International Business is the study of the cross-border trade, investments and corporate functions by firms, and the role of national governments and international institutions in regulating these activities.  The course examines the objectives and strategies by multinationals in internationalization and the strategic choices in country locations, market entry, product/service offerings, organisational structure & human resource management.  Related topics include the international business environment (economic, cultural, political, legal), globalisation, foreign direct investments, licensing, franchising, foreign entry modes, strategic alliances, and regional economic integration.  The course will demonstrate the challenges for business and management in an international environment.
graduateOutcomes: Understanding of global and Asian perspectives
Understanding of global and Asian perspectives

name: Intelligent Organisations

school.name: Lee Kong Chian School of Business

description: The course aims to nurture an intelligence mindset in interested students by introducing some basic concepts of Chaos, Complexity Theory (Complex Adaptive System) and Intelligent Organization Theory such as consciousness, intelligence, complexity, connectivity, dissipation, emergence, autopoiesis, self-organization, biodiversity, rugged landscape and dialogue, and how they can be better exploited by human/business organizations to increase their competitiveness in a knowledge-intensive and fast changing environment. The complex adaptive dynamics of the human thinking systems and their organizations, the nonlinearity of intelligence, and intelligence management will also be discussed. The concept of organizing around intelligence – the complexity-intelligence strategy and the significance of nurturing an intelligent organization with a biotic structure that encompasses an intense intelligence source (orgmind) will also be studied (intelligent organization theory). Additional significant and critical CAS/IO properties such as the edge of chaos, the butterfly effect, the red queen race, smarter evolvers, longer-term gain and their relationships with risk-taking, sustainability, and innovation and creativity will be explained. Ultimately, the course will cover the new and more holistic thinking/planning, such as the integrated deliberate and emergent strategy, and the intelligence leadership and management theory.

name: Enterprise Development

school.name: Lee Kong Chian School of Business

description:
Enterprise development is the process involved in managing the various stages in an enterprise with focus on the early phases of its life cycle, including the factors that contribute to its survival. 

This course will provide students with experiential learning opportunities in order to acquire the relevant knowledge and skills in running and growing a new business.

The following are some of the questions that will be addressed: 
a)	What do enterprises need to do during their startup phase?
b)	What are the key elements they need after surviving the startup phase? 
c)	How do they compete against others and keep themselves afloat?  
d)	How can any enterprise continue to grow and handle the issues faced in the midst of various challenging events?

name: Family Business

school.name: Lee Kong Chian School of Business

description:
Family businesses are the most prevalent form of business in the world. It is also an emerging and vibrant area of interest today among academics, practitioners and students of management. This course explores the unique challenges and opportunities involves in ownership and management of family businesses. Key family, ownership and management issues relevant to the management and continuity of these enterprises will be covered. Topics in this course include the uniqueness of family business, succession, governance, working with non-family managers, communication, strategy and continuity. 

This course will be useful to students from business-owning families. As most of the business organizations in Asia are family-owned, this course will also benefit students who may work for a family business in the course of their future career. Students who wish to enter the private banking, wealth management, corporate banking and consulting industry will find knowledge gained in this course helpful to their work. Anyone who thinks the interaction of two somewhat mutually exclusive systems – the family and the business - difficult will find this course fascinating.
graduateOutcomes: Understanding of global and Asian perspectives

name: Sustainable Entrepreneurship

school.name: Lee Kong Chian School of Business

description: Sustainable entrepreneurship is increasingly important as communities, institutions, and individuals seek new ways to address societal and environmental needs that are not adequately met by existing systems. In this course, students will learn concepts, frameworks, and practical skills to design commercially viable ventures that create meaningful impact.The course is organised around the development and evaluation of sustainable ventures. Students will learn to view a new venture as an interconnected system of choices, where changing one part of the system can reshape the whole business model. They will experience how placing sustainability and impact at the core of a venture can lead to new ways of creating, delivering, and capturing value. Students will therefore learn to work as both venture builders and venture evaluators: designing sustainable ventures while also judging whether their commercial and impact logic is credible.
areas: Public Pol and Public Mgmt Electives
graduateOutcomes: Understanding of global and Asian perspectives

name: Management of Innovation

school.name: Lee Kong Chian School of Business

description:
In knowledge economies for firms to succeed and grow the entrepreneurial behaviour has to shift from opportunity seeking to opportunity creation. Innovation and creativity have thus become critical to firm survival. Policy makers and businesses in Singapore have taken a conscious decision to accelerate the process and move into knowledge-based industries.

This course is designed to introduce students to the managerial systems and processes, which are being introduced by firms to manage innovations in a knowledge economy. Innovation management as a concept is often viewed as an extension to management of technology. This course, however, will addresses the subject from the organizational perspective and will cover a broad range of issues relating to organizational structure, organizational culture, business systems, small firm networks and knowledge management. The course will clarify concepts through readings and cases. Students will be introduced to tools and techniques available and exposed to innovation management software. Further to aid experiential learning students will undertake a project.

name: Leadership Seminar with CEOs

school.name: Lee Kong Chian School of Business

description:
This course is designed to give students opportunities to interact with about 10 CEOs/MDs during the semester. The invited speakers will share with students their views on leadership and management.

Before each CEO session, class will meet to analyze the transforming power of leadership and how its practice changes individuals, organizations and societies.  Students will examine different perspectives of leadership in the business world as well as in politics and the arts.   They will learn how leadership is developed in different organizational and cultural settings and how it is portrayed in different media including films, plays and novels. 

Are great leaders born or made? Can training or coaching make a difference? This course analyses the transforming power of leadership and how its practice changes individuals, organizations and societies. It seeks to expose students to different perspectives of leadership in the business world as well as in politics and the arts.

It will examine how leadership is developed in different organizational and cultural settings and how it is portrayed in different media including films, plays and novels. The focus of the course will not be on the identification of critical leadership traits or tasks but on the interactions between a leader, the organization and the context in which leadership evolves. Weekly CEO talks will form an integral part of the course.
areas: General Educatn (Not Appl for Intake 2015 onwards)

name: Strategic Management in China

school.name: Lee Kong Chian School of Business

description: The primary topic of this course is strategic management in the Chinese context, including that of both local Chinese companies and foreign companies operating in China, but with a somewhat greater focus on the former. The course has two primary features. First, it broadly encompasses three levels of strategies of companies competing in the Chinese context: business strategies, corporate strategies, and cross-border competitive strategies. Second, in analyzing the strategies of companies competing in the Chinese context, the course will take a comparative perspective. The key frameworks in strategic management are mostly developed in the West. Since there are fundamental differences in macro national environment, competitive industry, and firm strategic issues between China and the West, whether the existing frameworks are applicable to the Chinese context is thus a key concern. We shall discuss throughout the course the similarities and differences between strategic management issues in the West and in China.

name: Sustain Mgmt & Governance

school.name: Lee Kong Chian School of Business

description: This course provides an introduction to environmental sustainability and human development issues, and the means of framing, analysing and solving such problems. As environmental and social problems mount around the world, firms have become more attuned to the need to devise new products, services and strategies, and to communicate these to a variety of stakeholders, even as they cooperate with them.Environmental sustainability, and more generally, sustainability, has become increasingly important to developed and developing nations alike. Typical issues include resource scarcity and polluted environments, but more recently, global climate change has become the primary issue for many. In general, sustainability issues often consist of complex interactions between human activity and the environment. The course will apply several academic perspectives to characterizing these problems and their possible solutions. The course will focus in particular on businesses’ role in causing and addressing sustainability problems and on how they moderate their impacts. An important part of addressing the sustainability of firms is the employment of various concepts and frameworks that help incorporate the sustainability perspective into firms’ strategies and operations. To help characterize firms’ sustainability and determine appropriate courses of action, the course will cover specific managerial tools and frameworks. The primary focus will be on strategy and business models that support change and its operationalization, but the course will also illustrate the role that “greening” other business functions play in the sustainability of the firm, including those of marketing, supply chains, and financing. The course will review core management frameworks to help non-business major students become familiar with more sustainability-specific frameworks, practices and concepts to be covered. These tools are not only means for improving a firm’s sustainability performance, but also support its transparent and effective reporting. Representative examples of sustainability measurement standards will be introduced and their potential impacts in advancing corporate sustainability will be discussed. The course will also reflect on the general role of innovation in all of this. Technology issues covered include the role of information technology in addressing poverty, and solutions that reorganize the industrial system (e.g. renewable energy policies, and industrial ecosystems or industrial symbiosis, i.e., industries that incorporate recycling loops at regional levels).
areas: Public Pol and Public Mgmt Electives
tracks: PLE: Public Policy and Governance Track

name: Mng Strat Chg & Dig Transfn
longName: Managing Strategic Change and Digital Transformation

school.name: Lee Kong Chian School of Business

description: To achieve superior performance in an increasingly dynamic and uncertain global business environment, companies in every industry must create internal capability to harness strategic change for sustainable competitive advantage. However, companies that are able to strategically change their entrenched ways of doing things and then reclaim leading positions are the exception rather than the rule. With the industry 4.0 upon us and fast advancement in digital technologies, firms in many industries would find it even more pressing but challenging to build the managerial capabilities to cope with the digital transformation that will reshape the business landscape tremendously for the future. Against this backdrop, this course discusses how companies can effectively manage the strategic change and digital transformation that will significantly impact the way the business is configured for competitive advantage. Besides the internal managerial challenge, the course also emphasizes that companies must cope with strategic interactions with different industry players to create value collectively and continuously. With respect to digital transformation, the course discusses digital concepts and technologies such as omni-channel, platforms, eco-systems, blockchain, IOT, AI, and cloud computing etc. that impose both challenges and opportunities for strategic change management in the increasingly technology-based, internet-based, and data-based business contexts.

name: Play in Dsgn & Cultural Invntn
longName: Play in Design and Cultural Invention

school.name: Lee Kong Chian School of Business

description:
This course will explore how ‘play’ can enhance creative design processes to promote innovation and invention. Play was borne out of not only human desires for leisure and frivolity, but cultural and biological needs such as learning and community bonding. Recently, it has been observed that inventors in history have conceived of new ideas and products, even technological inventions, in a playful manner (Johnson, 2016). Playful invention processes could be serious experimental (and risky) efforts, or playfully frivolous ones. The course will analyze and apply creative and inventive processes, with the focus on how the mind can explore more widely and inventively by becoming less self-conscious and critical through play. 

Playful invention facilitates creativity by blending ideas together from different domains, causing ‘forms’ to transcend boundaries, and ultimately, to reshape not only leisure, but other domains and culture itself. This creative blending helps cross-fertilize domains with new ideas. We will examine how inventors ‘playfully created’ in different domains such as narrative, visual arts, space (including architectural space), and games. While most of the cultural domains covered relate to historical and current popular culture, we also pay attention to specific local and ‘globalized national’ cultures.

At least half of the course focuses on the actual practice of techniques that are related to the conceptual study of domains and thinking processes. We will adapt the design thinking process to incorporate additional brainstorming techniques (including domain-specific ideation techniques) and user-centered prototyping while removing the ‘project client’ typically seen in design thinking projects. In addition, we will illustrate and practice how to design using domains as lenses into the design of forms related to those domains. 

A significant part of the course will involve a project to design an innovative experience or other ‘form’ using these creativity and design techniques. In-class (or online) group exercises and projects will be used to demonstrate and practice these techniques, and full class attendance is expected in order to participate in these group exercises and group work.

name: Nego Early Stg Startup Financg

school.name: Lee Kong Chian School of Business

description:
This course aims to equip aspiring entrepreneurs with a basic toolkit to steer a startup through the quagmire of raising external capital from venture capital investors while protecting the interests of the founding team and your employees.  

Through real-world term sheet negotiation exercises and other practical exercises, students will go through the entire fundraising process from evaluating different external fund-raising opportunities and identifying the appropriate investors for the business, reviewing and negotiating term sheets, scaling up with various stakeholders and navigating a startup to a successful exit.  It aims to put the aspiring student founder on an even playing field when negotiating across and working with sophisticated venture capital investors in building a successful startup that creates value in Southeast Asia’s growing startup ecosystem.
graduateOutcomes: Understanding of global and Asian perspectives

name: Fraud Protection for Entre

school.name: Lee Kong Chian School of Business

description: This course equips aspiring entrepreneurs, social entrepreneurs, and managers with essential tools for understanding and identifying instances of fraud, with a view to developing a fraud risk management strategy for their new venture. It aims to provide students with a working knowledge of the various types of fraudulent conduct and the legal framework in place to prevent and deter instances of fraud. In addition, to learning from past cases of fraud, the course also explores new forms or methods of fraud that can arise from new technologies.

name: Spec Top in Mgmt

school.name: Lee Kong Chian School of Business

description: This course covers a specific topic related to management and strategy by an instructor who will change from one topic to another. The course chose such topics as Management in Asia Context, Management in Japan, and High-Tech Business Development in the past by the different instructors.  This course caters to students who are interested in topics that are not covered by regular undergraduate courses.

name: Country Studies/BSM

school.name: Lee Kong Chian School of Business

description: The course incorporates a planned visit to one or more cities/countries in Asia, so that students may get a better appreciation of the business  and socio-cultural environment of the cities/countries studied. The course typically begins with a series of classes on campus and culminates in a short but intensive overseas trip. While overseas, visits are made to companies, NPOs, government agencies, and/or universities.
