name: Digital Business  WSE

school.name: Lee Kong Chian School of Business

description: This programme is a collaboration between SMU and a leading company in Singapore, offering SMU students a six-month extended internship experience. The partner company is from the Artificial Intelligence (AI) related or digital-related industries, or is engaging digital transformation with AI or digital technologies, Artificial intelligence and digital technologies are transforming business, government, and society rapidly and profoundly both in Singapore and beyond. More and more businesses are going digital and embracing an AI-driven transformation to enhance efficiency, growth and innovation. There is fast growing demand for talents that have up-to-date ideas, skills, tools and solutions to help these organizations stay ahead of the curve in this AI/digital age. This work-study elective provides students with firsthand experience in digital business, allowing them to apply analytical frameworks and problem-solving techniques to AI-driven and digital transformation in a firm’s multiple functions including marketing, finance, operation, innovation, human resources management and strategic decision-making etc.Through this immersive experience, SMU students will:•	Gain hands-on exposure to real-world AI and digital related challenges across industries.•	Develop expertise in AI-driven business process reengineering, AI/digital business model, AI-driven decision-making, and digital transformation.•	Build strong industry connections that enhance their employability and career prospects.This elective is open to all Year 3 and Year 4 SMU students who meet the necessary criteria.  This programme equips students with practical skills and industry exposure, preparing them for exciting careers in AI or digital related businesses.
competencies: One or more business functions that are affected by digital technologies

name: I&E WSE

school.name: Lee Kong Chian School of Business

description: The Innovation & Entrepreneurship (I&E) Work-Study Elective (WSE) is a collaboration between SMU and organisations in the public and private sectors that are driving  innovation and/or entrepreneurial initiatives. This programme offers students the opportunity to undertake a 5-month extended internship, where they will contribute to real-world innovation and venture creation efforts.With an extended internship timeframe, students will be immersed in the partner organisation’s innovation processes, take on meaningful responsibilities, and develop entrepreneurial mindsets and skills such as opportunity recognition, creative problem-solving, lean experimentation, and agile execution. Overall, the WSE will equip students with practical knowledge and transferable skills to thrive in innovation-focused or entrepreneurial careers.The I&E WSE will take place locally, with students interning for at least four days each week and attending classes on campus up to one day a week. The internship duration will typically span a school term (e.g., August to December for Term 1 or January to May for Term 2).Students are strongly recommended to apply for the WSE only after their first year.

name: Strategic Mgmt WSE

school.name: Lee Kong Chian School of Business

description: This programme is a collaboration between SMU and leading companies across diverse industries, offering SMU students a five-month extended internship experience focused on strategic management.  In today’s rapidly evolving and competitive business environment, organizations are increasingly seeking individuals who can think strategically, anticipate market shifts, and drive sustainable growth. This work-study elective provides students with firsthand exposure to strategic planning and execution, enabling them to apply frameworks and tools to help organizations navigate uncertainty, seize new opportunities, and build long-term competitive advantage.Through this immersive experience, SMU students will:•	Gain real-world exposure to strategic challenges across various sectors.•	Apply strategic analysis, industry research, and problem-solving skills to real business contexts.•	Build meaningful professional networks that strengthen career readiness and job opportunities.This elective is open to all Year 3 and Year 4 SMU students who meet the necessary criteria.  The programme equips students with practical strategic thinking capabilities, positioning them for future roles in corporate strategy, business development, consulting, and innovation management.
graduateOutcomes: Understanding of global and Asian perspectives

name: Management,Leadership & Ethics
description:
A good understanding of how individuals and groups behave in organizations will give accounting professionals a competitive advantage at the workplace. This course adopts a managerial approach in understand how people behave and act in organizations. It informs participants on the various theories and good practices in the human dimension of organizations. It aims to help accounting professionals develop essential managerial and leadership competencies for high performance in today’s work environment.  

The course introduces participants to a broad range of managerial and leadership issues. Topics covered include: self awareness, stress management, creative thinking problem solving, ethical reasoning, leadership power, ethical leadership, motivation, performance management, team-building, communications, conflict management, managerial ethics and change management.

name: Strategy
description: This course deals with major techniques and approaches to the development and implementation of corporate strategy. This course explores the underlying concepts, analytical techniques, and evaluation of strategic options that form the basis for strategic analysis and action. This course is designed to introduce you to the real world of strategy and to explore the reasons for the success and failure of businesses in this era of global competition.

name: Strategy
description: This course is designed to study strategy and related issues that affect the success of the entire organization. This course introduces the theory and tools of critical and effective strategic analysis, and thinking. This seminar concentrates on current theoretical and empirical research relating to emerging areas of knowledge in the strategic management field. It reflects the emphasis of current research on strategic and organizational phenomena.

name: Strategy & Organisation
description: This course is designed to teach strategy and the organizational changes, and leadership necessary to create competitive success. A key aspect of strategic success is execution, without which ideas remain only ideas and not vehicles for value creation. The topics of execution by way of the organization, management and change leadership will be discussed in detail. Lectures, case studies, readings, simulations, tools and their practical use, as well as class participation will be the primary vehicle to create the appropriate learning environment. The outcome of this course will be an effective theoretical and practical understanding by the students of strategic analysis, formulation, execution, and the role and practice of leadership, management and organization.

name: Entrepreneurship & Business Cr
description: This course aims to introduce the students to the concept and value of entrepreneurship in a wider context, the theoretical models and practice of entrepreneurial process and their application in various organizational contexts. It seeks to develop a critical understanding of key issues in entrepreneurship, including implications of entrepreneurship, paths to entrepreneurship, and environments for entrepreneurship. Participants will analyze theoretical and practical arguments on entrepreneurial opportunities, strategies and tools for various types of entrepreneurial processes and management. They will compare and contrast different theoretical approaches to entrepreneurship and enterprise development in different types of organizations.

name: Management Theory
description: This course provides an understanding of the foundational concepts and empirical studies in management. It surveys the development of management theories and an analysis of the current trends in management thoughts. It examines how scholars construct theories to explain organizational phenomena. The course will review basic writings, research and theories on management. In the light of the vast body of knowledge, only selected issues of interest in the management field will be explored in depth.

name: Introduction to Research
description: This course introduces students to the foundations of research design for management research. It will explore selection of the research question, research design, literature review, and writing and publishing management research. It will introduce selected qualitative methods for data collection and analysis such as ethnography, interviewing, observation, and computer-aided methods of data analysis; and selected quantitative methods for data collection such as experiments, surveys, and secondary data analysis. At the end of the course, the participants should have prepared a draft of their thesis proposal.

name: Social Entrepreneurship
description: Social entrepreneurship examines the process of creating new independent or corporate ventures that pursue the dual primary missions of social benefit and financial return on investment. Hence, the course concerns itself with nonprofit organisations and for profit ventures that have a social mission and aim to be financially self-sufficient or are profit driven. This course is designed as an introduction to the field. It examines the obstacles and constraints faced by social entrepreneurs, a nd surfacing new strategies for them. The course will draw on practitioners as well as on historical and contemporary models to explore the unique range of issues and challenges facing the new social venture. The course invites students to explore solutions to societal problems and to evaluate the market opportunities for social venture creation, the social capital markets and the trade off between social and financial returns, and resource issues. The course will examine the unique management and marketing strategies for the growing social venture. The research seminars will cover the areas of enquiry in nonprofit management and the differences between social entrepreneurship and traditional management and innovation.

name: Intl Business Research Seminar
description: This research seminar supplements MGMT205 “International Business”.  The principal aim of this seminar is to overview the academic literature and research methods in International Business.  The seminar introduces participants to seminal papers and to current trends in International Business research.   In the process, seminar participants will learn to formulate relevant research questions, design research methods, and review academic papers in the field of International Business.

name: Qualitative Research Methods
description:
This course introduces students to qualitative research methods. Qualitative methods refers to a variety of research techniques that are non-statistical in nature, involve gathering data first hand from “primary sources” (i.e. by observing or interviewing people or organizations), and form a complementary research approach to statistical and other quantitative techniques. Qualitative methods help researchers develop insights into new phenomena, into process, and into complex relationships that are not easily ascertained with other methods. 

The course will introduce qualitative methods from four perspectives. One is by formally studying and practicing the practices of the methods. The second is by studying formative qualitative pieces of research. The third is by understanding the strengths of qualitative research, in studying complex systems with interacting actors or subsystems, and in studying process. The fourth is by examining some of the techniques (as practiced in the real world) in contrast to how they might be practiced (or adapted) to other, specifically virtual, worlds.

name: Quantitative Research Methods
description:
A large proportion of contemporary research on organization, strategy, and management relies on quantitative research methods. This course is designed to provide the statistical background and to familiarize the students with some of the commonly used quantitative research techniques, including ordinary least squares multivariate regression, models for binary outcomes, count models, and pooled cross-section/time series analysis. 

The main objective of this course is to help students understand the relationship between theory, data and statistical methods. This is not a course in statistical theory (i.e. we will not be deriving likelihood functions etc.) but a course on the practical use of statistical techniques to answer management related research questions. We will spend considerable time thinking about theoretical insights that can be translated into testable propositions, and how these propositions are best tested. We will do this through discussions of published papers from leading journals or high quality working papers in management research, and by having you solve statistical problems, work with data and estimate models. At the end of the course, you should be able to use common statistical methods to ask and answer research questions, and have developed critical skills in evaluating others’ research, such that you may apply these skills to your own thesis and other research works.

name: Career Management Skills
description: The course is aimed at developing skills and competencies for managing and developing one’s career; the job hunting process and thriving in a career and job in the Singaporean context.

name: Operations Management
description: When companies produce and deliver goods or services to meet customer demand, they do so by executing business processes.  In this course, students discover how business processes can be designed, analyzed and improved to lift the performance of any organization, whether it is a bank, a hospital, a resort, or a fashion retailer.  The course reveals how process management skills can be used to reduce costs, lower inventories, cut waiting times, improve quality, enhance service levels, and increase revenues and company profits.  Specifically, students will gain practical knowledge of process design, demand forecasting, capacity planning, workflow planning and control, quality management, and lean operations. With a focus on the basic concepts that govern process management, the course also provides the necessary foundation to pursue further development in operations and supply chain management.
graduateOutcomes: Understanding of global and Asian perspectives

name: Operations Management
description: When companies produce and deliver goods or services to meet customer demand, they do so by managing operations, in other words by  executing business processes.   In this course, students discover how business processes can be designed, analyzed and improved to lift the performance of any organization, whether it is a bank, a hospital, a resort, or a fashion retailer.  The course reveals how process management skills can be used to reduce costs, lower inventories, cut waiting times, improve quality, enhance service levels, and increase revenues and company profits.   Specifically, students will gain practical knowledge of process design, demand forecasting, capacity planning, workflow planning and control, quality management, and lean operations. With a focus on the basic concepts that govern process management, the course also provides the necessary foundation to pursue further development in operations and supply chain management.

name: Enterprise Growth and Devt
description: Many new ventures experience failure during growing their businesses—Growth creates new challenges that have to be met. This course considers the growth stages of the firm beyond the startup and survival phase. In the growth of the new venture, both the firm and its founder(s) are likely to go through some considerable transitions. We focus on managerial issues during different phases of the new venture’s expansion and transitions and offer management tools that are needed to capture value from entrepreneurial activities and to build a new venture into a significant enterprise.

name: Corporate Communication
description: The main goal of this course is first to introduce culture as a value-relevant aspect in international business; secondly, the course aims to prepare executives to become agents of international change and intercultural exchange.

name: Corporate Strategy
description:
The Strategic Management course develops the skills managers need to analyze and improve business performance.  It focuses on competitive advantage and how firms may achieve, sustain, extend and renew it.   Competitive advantage depends on coordinated, mutually reinforcing actions across the entire organization. As a result, the course takes a top management perspective from which the logic of interaction among the functional areas – such as marketing, operations, and finance – may be evaluated and reconfigured.   Both environmental and firm specific sources of performance differences among firms are examined by drawing on a wide body of theory, evidence, and practice.  The course emphasizes the examination of specific cases and the development of practical recommendations as well as communication and persuasion.
This course is a blend of theory and practice where the emphasis is on integrating insights from other functional and core courses to diagnose the reasons for current organizational performance and to develop coordinated actions that will increase future organizational performance by:
1.	Analyzing environmental and structural variables which directly impact organizational performance.
2.	Assessing the motivations and options of competitors.
3.	Evaluating the quality and quantity of available resources. 
4.	Developing plausible resource reconfigurations (strategic options) 
5.	Assessing and choosing among plausible options, taking implementability and projected relevant events into account.

name: Corporate Strategy
description: This course introduces students to the theoretical concepts and analytical tools required for formulating and implementing appropriate strategies that affect the enduring success of the entire organization. Topics covered include external and internal environmental analyses, business-level strategies, corporate-level strategies, strategy process and implementation, and special topics such as competitive dynamics and competition in high tech industries. This course emphasizes the application of theory to the real world strategic issues. Students are encouraged to synthesize their existing knowledge and experience in various industries into a comprehensive understanding of strategy.

name: Glob. Econ: Issue & Challenges
description: This course provides students with an understanding of the major changes and developments in the global economy and the key challenges arising from globalization. Such understanding is essential in assessing the business and political risks in the global business environment. Students will gain a practical knowledge of key changes affecting international trade, cross-border labor and capital flows, monetary policy, exchange rates and the global financial sector development, as well as the roles that governments, central banks and multilateral institutions play in these changes.
graduateOutcomes: Understanding of global and Asian perspectives

name: Doing Good Doing Well
description:
Making money is good.  So is reaching out to help impoverished individuals and communities.  It is right to support ‘green’ initiatives and it is right for local business to become an active contributor in the community.  But can we do it all?  Many successful businesses argue that we can.  They argue not only that we CAN invest socially but that we MUST . . .  if we, as corporations, are to maintain our ‘license to operate.’   In this broad survey course, we look at the innovative ways traditional for-profit corporations are reinventing themselves as social leaders.  We also look at the innovative ways not for profits are leveraging business methods to improve their service delivery and enhance sustainability.  We also look at the myriad forms of ‘social’ enterprise that now exist, i.e. at the organization that are neither businesses nor not for profits but something in between.

This course is recommended for all who would like a comprehensive introduction to social enterprise and corporate social responsibility (CSR) and/or for those who would like to understand what the new ‘social mandate’ means for traditional business operations.  The course is especially appropriate for those who aspire to senior leadership positions and who recognize the ‘social’ role they and their companies will be forced to play in today’s demanding market environment.  Collectively, the class will review and debate the various CSR experiments that are underway today, consider the profit impact of these initiatives, and consider their social value and sustainability.  The class will also consider how to create, implement, and assess CSR initiatives that generate strategic synergies with traditional business operations.   As a broad survey, the course will also investigate Bottom of the Pyramid business methods and social enterprise development

name: Managing Technological Change
description:
Managing Technological Change examines primarily larger strategic issues in environments altered by technologies. As the range and scale of the impacts of technological change is vast, the course will necessarily be selective. It will be organized around three important and distinct areas which are affected by technological change – the products and services which use new technologies, the competitive markets in which firms compete using the technologies and the organizations which must develop and execute new strategies while taking technological change into account.  These three areas are interdependent in the sense that changes in one can require coordinated changes in the other.  

The first section of the course introduces the idea that technological changes can be very different -- both in their impact on the competitive environment, and in how they affect individual firms.  Different types of technological change place different stresses on firms and some are more difficult to adapt to than others.  For example, the logic of the technology may dictate that some standard be established.  Or, the technology may make existing knowledge of customers and their preferences largely obsolete.

The second section of the course is more centrally concerned with classic strategic issues in product-markets  --- how firms create and capture value and how they build capabilities to compete over the longer term.  For example, if the firm can create value with a new product, can it reap the rewards without control over distribution channels or must it also invest in these? 

The third section of the course considers the organizational variables associated with technological competition. Firms struggle to both extend their existing technologies and product market positions while also creating new businesses. Organizational innovations from internal start-ups to mergers and acquisitions to corporate venture capital must complement, and may lead, an overall technology strategy.

name: Agile and Disruptive Strategy
description: This module touches on disruptive innovation and industry transformation. Participants will look at business model innovation, creating market-appropriate customer value proposition, business model innovation in emerging market, effective strategy execution (managing complexity and unexpected), and developing non-market strategy to shape value system for disruptive innovation.

name: Innovation & Growth Management
description:
Necessity is the mother of invention. One reason for firms to innovate is the necessity to re-invent themselves and get out of stagnation: the industry has either gotten obsolete, or competitors have adopted newer and more efficient business models, and products or services based on more advanced technologies. Innovation is then a necessity as the firm has to innovate or perish, one only has to look at what happened to Blockbuster and Kodak. Blockbuster at one point of time was the leading media rental firm in the world, but they chose to ignore innovation in the way they were delivering their media content to customers. As Netflix gained scale, Blockbuster’s inability to innovate meant that their business model was obsolete, and they had no choice but to file for bankruptcy. Kodak is another famous example: Steven Sasson at Kodak invented the digital camera way back in the 1970s, but rather than developing and commercializing the innovation, Kodak chose to put the new technology on the backburner, as its commercialization would have meant that their existing business model that relied on chemical printing of photographs would have to be cannibalized. However, other competitors jumped on the bandwagon for competitive advantage: hence, if you do not pursue innovation, your competitors will make you obsolete someday, no product or business model has an eternal shelf life. Innovation has many dimensions: it creates value for existing customers, thereby letting you keep your current market share; it creates value for new customers, enabling you to get growth; it enables you to work with new processes to access a lower cost base; supplier innovation enables you to leverage partners’ innovation capabilities to offer value to customers, and capture value for yourself. So the notion of continuous improvement is indeed extendable to continuous innovation, the business world in all sectors moves on a treadmill; the pace of the treadmill is faster in some industries like technology and fashion, and slower in some other industries. Innovation is the lever that enables you to keep pace on the treadmill if you are at the industry average; and enables you to set the pace if you innovate at a faster rate than the industry average. If you stand still on the treadmill or run at a slower pace than the treadmill in a competitive environment, at some stage, you will be thrown off the treadmill.

This course should be of particular interest to people aspiring for a career in designing and managing for innovation, either directly (e.g., V.P. of R&D, R&D Manager) or indirectly (e.g., management consulting). The course will also be useful to SME proprietors and entrepreneurs who intend to serve new markets, or use new technologies, or participants who wish to strategically reposition their offerings in an existing market. The course should also be of interest to people who manage interfaces between innovation and business functions such as finance, marketing, managerial accounting and human resources.
graduateOutcomes: Understanding of global and Asian perspectives

name: Evaluating Entrepreneurial Opp
description: This half-credit course is an introductory course in entrepreneurship focused of evaluating new business ideas.  Why should you take this class? If you are interested in pursuing entrepreneurship as a career choice or leading new business development in a corporation, this course will introduce you to the typical problems and solutions in new business creation. Furthermore most individuals go through spells of unemployment or self-employment during which the ability to evaluate opportunities may prove useful.

name: Execution-The Art of  Perf Mgt
longName: Execution - The Art of  Performance Management
description:
Execution.  It is the essence of management.  It is about getting product out the door.  It is about ensuring excellence in customer service.  It is about ensuring staff are trained and on-board.  In this interactive course, participants will invest in developing the tools and capabilities they need to lead organizations that truly work.  Specifically, students will learn how to develop and use the strategic performance management systems that guide and reward action.  Throughout the course, we will consider not just the technical structures of these systems but how they are used to ensure:  AWARENESS of strategic intent, UNDERSTANDING of how that strategy is implemented, COMMITMENT to that strategy, and ACTION that yield results.
	
Collectively, we will focus on how to translate strategy into actionable measurement systems, how to build and communicate those measurement systems throughout the firm,  how to monitor and ‘refresh’ those systems, and how to motivate employee action by linking personal incentives to realization of specific measured goals.  Again, while much attention will be paid to the technical construction of these systems, this is not a finance or accounting course.   Performance measures have little impact unless they are reinforced by the leaders of the organization.   To ensure effective use of these systems, students will also learn how to anticipate, recognize, and respond to the leadership challenges that arise in complex organizations and how to serve as inspirational figures within their companies.

name: Intl Strategic Mgmt Simulation
description: To study strategic management is one thing, to implement it successfully is another. Strategic games such as this International Strategic Management Simulation are valuable transitional tools for translating business school concepts into the real world. The course simulates the strategy formulation and implementation process of top management teams. Teams will collect many different types of managerially relevant data, analyze it, make decisions, and observe the results in a competitive environment where international rival teams are doing the same. As a group, teams will meet to adjust their plans, expectations and overall strategy in light of their results and their anticipation of future conditions and the actions of their competitors. The course is designed to support SMU’s focus on teaching integrative managerial skills by simulating a more complete business decision-making environment.  Effective management practice requires the effective combination of specialized analysis and information, usually in teams, to make streams of related and ideally, mutually supportive decisions over time.  The simulation will provide a learning experience in which such skills in integrating diverse information and perspectives can be developed.

name: International Business
description: This course introduces you to the complexity of managing an organisation that is operating in geographically dispersed and legally, institutionally, socio-economically and culturally diverse environments. Managing international business is an expansive topic with a broad scope as it entails dealing with multiple functions (e.g. research and development, human resource management, supply chain management, production, servicing, and marketing) concurrently in multiple regions of a multinational enterprise (MNE). You will learn to understand the challenges facing MNEs as well as the relevant strategies they employ.

name: Leading Entre. & Innovation
description:
Perhaps no business subject is surrounded by more interest, mystique, or deification than innovation and its entrepreneurial roots.  Industries and economies are forged by its presence; organizations are obsessed with being associated with it, the world changes when it really happens—and usually in unexpected ways. Truly, to create value where it did not exist prior is a noble pursuit, but is success found only with a few, or only with luck? 

In this course we examine the practice of innovation and entrepreneurship.  We define entrepreneurship more broadly to reflect a more realistic view:  that entrepreneurship is a management practice that can be understood and practiced.  The scope of the discussion includes entrepreneurial views where its participants act as promoters; as well as intrapreneurial views where its participants act as trustees.  Concepts and tools of ideation, innovation and solution development are woven into the practice and leadership of entrepreneurship:

1) The Entrepreneurial Manager 
     a. Role
     b. Behavior
     c. Leadership Attributes 
     d. Promoters v. Trustees
2) Ideation & Innovation
     a. Creative Process
     b. Innovation Process & Diffusion
     c. Solution development
3) Opportunity Assessment & Business Models
4) Managing Uncertainty & Growth

The discussion will be centered on published case studies and instructor developed case material.  Articles and text in support of the theories and frameworks of innovation will be part of the support material.  Tools, simulators and guest speakers will enhance the discussion and learning but it is the student’s perspective and contribution that add the greatest value, and as such, participation is a key learning method.

name: Managing Growing Business
World Environmental Issues
description: Environmental knowledge is crucial for any business leader today. Climate change, conservation efforts, alternative energies for oil replacement, contingency planning for sea level changes, are just some of the environmental issues reported in the media. But what are the hard scientific data behind the reporting? To make informed decisions, accurate information about the facts is necessary, but the facts are not always easily distilled from media reports that may be biased by advocacy. This course will use data on globally important environmental issues drawn directly from science. We will discuss the data and learn how to interpret them for business decisions. In many areas there may actually be a choice of action with different trade offs depending on the business or policy decisions taken. The goal of the course is to inform future business leaders with factual knowledge about global environmental issues, and to distinguish data from advocacy.

name: Connecting Art and Business
description:
The art market is growing spectacularly and evolving constantly. From 2003-2007/8, the art market experienced the greatest boom it has ever seen both in terms of volume and value, and auction houses recorded sales amounting to several hundred million dollars in a single night. Power has been shifting between established market players, opening new opportunities for artists, intermediaries and collectors alike. The development of art markets in China and India envisages a future of increasing globalization of the art market. This course gives a theoretical and practical introduction to the art market. Participant will develop an understanding of mechanisms of the art market by focusing on:

1.	An understanding of how the art world operates
2.	An insight into current art market strategies and developments
3.	The appropriate application of strategies and methodologies for doing  business in the art market

name: Managing for Value
longName: Managing for Value - Formulating Successful Business Strategies
description:
Most business leaders try and deliver against various important corporate objectives - driving top line growth, return on investment, cost competitiveness, customer satisfaction etc. Some of these objectives range from tactical moves to inspiring statements, but none of them can stand up to the scrutiny of a governing objective.  

Company resources should be managed to make them worth more than they would be if managed in any other way, by any other firm.

Managing for value or Value based management has been implemented as a governing objective for business strategy implementation by some of the best known FMCG companies – Coke, Pepsi, Cadbury, Unilever to name a few. This is indeed a very demanding objective which continuously drives businesses to weigh options and make choices.

The implementation process is resource intensive, structured and thorough.

This course will provide –

•A comprehensive overview on why MFV is considered one of the most proven and successful governing objective

•How does this principle translate in creation of actual business strategies – strategic position assessment, competitive strategy, participation strategy, pricing and operating strategy

•Through case studies clarify how it is actually implemented in the Industry

name: Blue Ocean Stgy & Value Inno
longName: Blue Ocean Strategy and Value Innovation
description:
Blue oceans are defined by untapped market space, demand creation, and the opportunity for highly profitable growth. Examples of the Blue Oceans are Wii and Yellowtail Winery to name but a few. 

In blue oceans, competition is irrelevant because the rules of the game are waiting to be set. 

In an ever-increasing number of industries, supply exceeds demand. This leads to a highly contested space as rivals fight for limited market share leading to bloody red oceans. Innovative leaders of tomorrow will become more concerned with generating blue oceans than in dominating pre-existing space. 

In this course, students will learn about Blue Ocean theory and Value Innovation methodology. They will:

-	Gain insight into why customer centric philosophies are unlikely to provide significant growth
-	Understand why organizations unwittingly ‘kill’ innovation
-	Discover how the Blue Ocean Strategy approach surfaces unfulfilled demand and uncontested markets
-	Learn how companies apply the Blue Ocean Strategy approach to out-achieve their corporate growth objectives.

name: Turning Concepts into Bus Case
longName: Innovation Development: Turning Concepts into Business Cases
description: This course introduces students to the basic conceptual frameworks and tools for translating “ideas” into concepts and making a business case out of them. To achieve these objectives, the students will go through readings to take into account the innovation processes and experiences of successful firms in different industries and also view things from the perspective of an entrepreneur. The course will be taught in the form of lectures and in-depth case study discussions. The students are expected to carefully read the assigned cases and come prepared to class.

name: Ethics,Risk,Crisis, Media Mgmt
description:
Ethics and Legal issues 
- Professional conduct.
- Access and use of (patient) data and research results.

Risk Management (Enterprise)
- Strategic.
- Operational.
- Financial.
- Reputational.

Crisis Management
- Business Continuity Planning.
- Disaster and Crisis Management.

Media Management
- Handling the Media.
- Cultivate media relations.

name: Corp Social Responsibility
description:
Traditional economists argue the central and sole goal of a business is to maximize returns to shareholders. A weakness with this mindset is that it puts profits above all else and thereby ignores that companies are social organizations that serve employees, suppliers, and communities in which they operate. This profit-only mindset can raise significant problems when companies do not view their mission in a wider context, such as illustrated by BP and the oil spill disaster, and at worst be the seed of destruction for amoral firms like Enron. 

This module explores the compelling reasons behind businesses taking on a broader role in developing social value that extends beyond the role of the firm as viewed by traditional economists. The module provides ideas, conceptual frameworks and tools to help students assess approaches to social value alignment and different models of interaction between corporations, governments, intergovernmental organizations, investors, and non-governmental organizations (NGOs). 

This module is practitioner-oriented and intended to provide the participants with a basis for working with and advising business leaders in developing strategic social value alignment, and engage customers through social marketing, and build and understanding of firm level social strategy, dynamics of relationships between companies and stakeholders. Leaders of non-profit and government agencies will also find the module of benefit as it covers public-private relationships and will help identify how to work with business leaders on areas of business responsibility. 

Social issues are wide a varied and include environmental management, health, education, social justice, labour standards, social mobility, climate change, and more. A full treatment of these topics is beyond the scope of this module. Instead, this module will provide broad frameworks and analytical tools for managing social value and stakeholder relationships, and provide illustrative examples though a guest speaker series to bring ideas to life. “Learning by doing” is the centre piece of this course which features a practicum style project where a team will work on realizing greater value for a firm they select to support.

name: Strategic Initiative Project
description:
Strategic Initiative Project is an approach that challenges you to learn through immersion in a real problem. It is a format that develops problem solving strategies and sector knowledge bases and skills by placing you in the active role of problem solvers confronted with an ill-structured situation that simulates the kind of problems you are likely to face as managers in complex organisations.

SIP makes a fundamental shift from a focus on teaching to a focus on learning. The process is aimed at using the power of authentic problem solving to engage you and enhance your learning and motivation. There are several unique aspects that define the SIP approach: Learning takes place within the contexts of currently occurring tasks, issues and problems. That is, these are truly real-world concerns.
graduateOutcomes: Understanding of global and Asian perspectives

name: Mg Growth in Midst of Change
longName: Managing Growth in the Midst of Change
description: This course explores the challenges managers face ensuring enterprise growth, be it in sales, size, results, scope and scale. The managers find their work compounded by changes that are taking place, within and outside their organizations. Where organizations are in their development will affect their growth.  Managers and entrepreneurs need to understand the challenges that affect firms at the various growth stages and the strategies that are appropriate. The firm might need to consider internationalization and cooperation with other firms. There is also a need to consider the interdependence between the various functional areas of management when growing an enterprise.

name: Innovation Management
description:
Even the mightiest of the market leaders have been humbled when they stopped creating innovations.  Innovation Management is central to new company formation or large firm’s growth strategy.  Many firms, both large and small are scrambling to recruit those in the know of innovation methodologies and innovation management as a means of future proofing their organizations. 

The course will provide:

1.	Understanding innovation.
2.	Innovation methodologies.
3.	Innovation Management.

name: Corp Strategy in a Global Env
longName: Corporate Strategy in a Global Environment
description:
Generally, strategy is defined as a set of choices that managers make in order to increase their firm’s performance relative to competitors. Corporate Strategy in a Global Environment considers strategic choices that managers make in the context of a multi-product, multi-business, multi-location firm. In this course, you will study how successful organizations choose, implement, and evaluate their strategy. The focus will lie on internal and external corporate growth strategies, which have become indispensable for success in today’s economic environment marked by increased globalization, rapid technological change, shortened product lifecycles, and enhanced competition. Tools and techniques for strategy formulation, implementation, and evaluation are discussed. Case studies are used to sharpen your understanding of the importance of strategic decision-making.

Specific areas of focus are:
- Corporate Strategy and Competitive Advantage
- Corporate Scope
- Growth through Acquisitions
- Global Strategy and International Expansion
- Sustaining a Successful Enterprise

name: Internship
description: It is an intentional supervised learning related to one's field of study and career goals. Internships can be a very structured learning experience or they can be designed to meet the expectations of the student. Internships can be done locally or overseas. They can be part-time or full-time, paid or unpaid. Internships can be done during the academic year. The one thing all good internship opportunities have in common is they provide students with career-related work experience. Internship is done for a 10 week period.

name: Network and Alliance Building
description: Alliances among companies have become a fundamental necessity for companies’ competitive and growth strategies. Firms use alliances for a variety of reasons – to share the risks or costs of entering into new products or markets, to access or learn relevant capabilities, to growth etc. At the same time, alliances are very difficult to manage and poorly conceived or managed alliances often create substantial problems for one or more of the alliance partners. Not surprisingly, more than half the alliances formed end up failing. Therefore, the goal of this program is to understand the benefits and risks that alliances create for individual companies and to learn how to form and manage alliances more successfully. This should help participants build their individual alliance skills as well as understand how their company can develop its organizational capability to manage alliances more effectively.

name: Business Study Mission
description: This course is designed to provide students with a rich understanding of business practices in a world region of great significance in global commerce – particularly for the future.  You will gain background knowledge of the history, culture, politics, and economics of South East Asia, followed by direct experience through a study tour to two important business centers in the area.

name: HRM for Tech & Ops Mgr
longName: HRM for Technology and Operations Manager
description: Welcome to the module on Human Resource Management for IT professionals. The aim of this module is to help you understand the importance of soft skills that must go hand in hand with technical competencies. Given the reality of globalization, this course attempts to highlight key areas that embrace the dynamics of self-management and working with others. Hence, the coverage spans over a broad range of topics designed to meet your needs at the workplace. We aim, therefore, to enhance the building of knowledge and relevant soft skills through seminars and the use of case studies, articles and self-assessment tools in order to develop personal and professional skills in working with others. The course is also intended to be interactive so as to foster a learning environment that facilitates creative thinking in the process of peer learning.

name: Executing Strategy
description: In this course we examine the analytic frameworks that can help managers identify viable strategies. These include competitive analysis and the analysis of strategic capabilities. We also study the process of strategy implementation and execution involving organisational issues such as leadership, culture and organisational structure. We use case studies to illustrate processes of strategy formulation and implementation.

name: Strategy
description: This course introduces students to the theoretical concepts and analytical tools required for formulating and implementing appropriate strategies that affect the enduring success of the entire organization. Topics covered include external and internal environmental analyses, business-level strategies, corporate-level strategies, strategy process and implementation, and special topics such as competitive dynamics and competition in high tech industries. This course emphasizes the application of theory to the real world strategic issues. Students are encouraged to synthesize their existing knowledge and experience in various industries into a comprehensive understanding of strategy.

name: Business Strategy & Org
description: This course introduces participants to the theoretical concepts and analytical tools required for formulating and implementing appropriate strategies that affect the enduring success of the entire organization. Topics covered include external and internal environmental analyses, business-level strategies, corporate-level strategies, strategy process implementation and organization.  This course emphasizes the application of theory to the real world strategic issues. Participants are encouraged to synthesize their existing knowledge and experience in various industries and backgrounds into a comprehensive understanding of strategy.

name: Leading Org Across Cultures
description:
With an increasingly globalized economy, leading and managing employees of different cultural backgrounds becomes imperative in organisations. This module takes the approach of understanding how culture differs and impacts on our interactions at the workplace in Asia and beyond. 

The course is broadly structured to enable an understanding of culture differences with an emphasis on how these similarities and differences impact workplace interactions. Through the course, students will:
(a) gain an understanding of their level of cultural competence at the individual level, 
(b) be given tools to analyze different culture patterns around the world and in particular, Asia, and; 
(c) learn to develop strategies for adapting to cultures with a view to managing in the organisational context. 

The emphasis of the module is on the interplay of cultural competence at the individual level, organisation culture dynamics at the workplace level and societal cultures at the national/country level.

name: Global Business Management
description: Many Global organizations manage their regional and global operations from Singapore. As the business environment is increasingly global, Multi-national corporations need to have staff and talent that understand global issues and possess a global mindset. This course will allow students to develop an understanding on the development of strategy, organizational capabilities, and management challenges faced by Multi-national Enterprises/Corporations (MNE/MNC) for operating in the global economy. We will study business challenges associated with developing strategies, implementing strategies, and managing the operations of companies whose activities stretch across national boundaries through cases, readings and articles. The course will train students to think about the multidisciplinary, multicultural and multilateral issues that are the critical to the management of a Global Enterprise – whether you are the frontline business manager, the country subsidiary manager, the global account manager, or the CEO. Where possible, we will use the Asian context and Asian cases studies that provide an Asian perspective. After this course, students will be more prepared to deal with key global challenges and management issues as Managers and Executives at Multi-national enterprises.

name: Creating & Capturing Value
longName: Innovation Workshop: Creating and Capturing Value
description:
The Innovation Workshop Modules are a central guided part of the learning experience, where students learn new ideas from the forefront of research and practice and create new ideas through cross-fertilization.  The purpose is to drive learning in the four key learning outcome themes in a way that allows many inputs from diverse sources, a key to creating an Idea ecosystem within the MI program.  Delivery of the Workshop occurs every Friday evening prior to Saturdays core module delivery.  A course coordinator manages the content of each Idea Workshop series.  It is not a seminar series, but rather a core set of topics centered around one of the 4 learning outcome themes.  Academic rigor is instilled by participation, papers, cases, simulation and/or exams for the assessed at term end.  Participation and attendance is required.  The purpose is provide as many inputs as possible to our students in the process of innovating across boundaries and existing domains.  There are 8 Innovation Workshop Modules per term.

Term 1 Innovation Workshops:  Creating & Capturing Value

o Session 1—Team Building in Innovation—Adel Dimian
o Session 2—Opportunity in Value creation—Desai Narasimhalu 
o Session 3—Design Thinking Frameworks I--Ted Tschang
o Session 4— Design Thinking Frameworks II--Ted Tschang
o Session 5—Creativity & Ideation I—Goh Ban Eng
o Session 6—Creativity & Ideation II—Goh Ban Eng
o Session 7—Architecting New Products & Services--Kelly Ingham
o Session 8—Negotiating for Value—Michael Benoleil

name: Opp. Recog., Idea & Innov Mgt
longName: Opportunity Recognition, Ideation and Innovation Management
description:
This course introduces the student to ‘the front end of innovation’. We will explore the theory and will practice Design Thinking, we will also apply the techniques and principles of design thinking through a project that will step through the ideation and opportunity recognition ‘front end’ of innovation. Design Thinking and the tools that support it are a powerful process that can improve product, service and experience concepts (selected applications to products and services will be covered). 

In Part 1, the design thinking process (based on the IDEO/Stanford Design School process) is introduced. This is a qualitative process consisting of the stages of: the observation of users, ideation, and prototyping. Iteration can occur between any steps, and multiple cycles are typical. Applications of design thinking to product and service innovation will be discussed, along with varying of the design contexts, including the private sector, government and social sectors. Design thinking will be framed against traditional innovation processes and other types of thinking. 

In Part 2, the course will cover theories of innovation management and how to make organizations more innovative.

name: The Innovator’s Mindset
description: This course delivers an understanding of how thinking occurs in the creative mind and organization. The student is led through the practical and theoretical frameworks of abductive thinking (the logic of what might be), inductive thinking (proving by observation that something works), and deductive thinking (proving by reason that something must be). Data collection and the interpretation of patterns and interactions are explored. The use of decision-making tools within these frameworks and game models elucidate the key learning outcomes.

name: Entrepren'l Fnce & New Bus Cr
description:
Welcome to the module on Entrepreneurial Finance & New Business Creation. In this course, we will examine the many and complex issues associated with finance and financial management in entrepreneurial organizations. Specifically, we will consider these four topics: Opportunity Identification, Valuation, Doing Deals and Harvesting. 

Opportunity Identification

We consider the myriad types of opportunities that might be recognized by an entrepreneurial and craft a framework for analyzing the nature of that opportunity.  We consider for example, the type of competitive advantage inherent in the opportunity, the potential cash requirements and returns of the project, its riskiness, its resource (especially human) requirements, and optimal timing.  

Valuation

The value of any project, asset, or organization is influenced by the magnitude, riskiness, and timing of its associated cashflow. In this section of the course, we examine the process of valuation, learning how to effectively project magnitude and riskiness of cashflows, and assess their optimal timing.   

Doing Deals

With the financial need and potential value of the organization clarified, the organization must next consider the source and cost of financing. In this section of the course, we look at the complex world of finance, working to understand the essential sources of finance, the myriad financial instruments available, and how final deals are struck.  

Harvesting

The final segment of the course will consider entrepreneurial exit. An often overlooked segment of the entrepreneurial business plan, defining a harvesting time frame and mechanism is essential for value maximization. We will consider the two most common vehicles for exit:  acquisitions and IPOs.

name: Managing Strat Innov & Change
description:
Day 1: Reddi
Brief description: How is strategic management different in knowledge intensive industries compared other industries? At first blush, not much. Hence, in session 1 we start with a review of core strategy concepts and frameworks. This review is brief. We will point you to readings should you want to refresh your memory or read more on the foundational concepts. More specifically we will ask: what is strategy; why and how to do industry structure analysis; In session 2 we cover generic strategies and we then turn to specific aspects of knowledge intensive industries like network externalities, the myth of first-mover advantage, consequences of winning the standard wars, the high degree of uncertainty surrounding in these industries that interact with core strategy concepts to provide a more nuanced application of the board core strategy frameworks. Evidence shows that several breakthrough inventions are made by large firms but not commercialized by them. The rigid mental models of managers, scientists in large firms makes them ignore architectural innovation which they dismiss as trivial innovation. The architectural innovation made by new firms end up swapping the market resulting in demise of established incumbents.

Day 2: Reddi
Then in session 3 we will focus on role of unique technology and capabilities of firm in determining resource allocation to new projects and extent and success of corporate diversification. In session 4 We also address why do large firms engage in acquisitions and how do they manage post acquisition IP which is mostly resident in individuals. Does the buyer firm keep the target firm as a standalone unit or does it integrate it? At the end of day 2 your group will have to present the group project.

Day 3: Adel
In the AM session we will discuss turnaround strategy and leadership using the HCA Hospice care case.  It will highlight the issues of leadership in a non profit and underscore leadership issues.
In the PM session we will discuss the innovation strategies of a Singapore firm trying to expand internationally.  Entry strategies and innovation challenges and micro political risk are explored.

name: Mach. Learnin for Deci Making
description:
The course is designed to guide MBA students in understanding and implementing data-driven decision-making in business contexts. It offers a step-by-step tutorial on constructing and applying machine learning algorithms for business problem-solving, utilizing Python.

Throughout the course, students will develop a comprehensive understanding of predictive analytics through both supervised (regression and classification) and unsupervised (clustering and dimensionality reduction) machine learning techniques. The course's real-world applications span a variety of business questions, from market segmentation to personalization, algorithmic trading, and portfolio management. Over eight weeks, it aims to make machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI) Accessible, Actionable, and Interpretable (AAI), turning these concepts into powerful tools for business problem-solving.

The course employs an interactive lecture format, where principles and applications of predictive analytics are explored, and a hands-on programming approach, where students engage directly with the material by completing parts of provided script templates.

This blend of conceptual and technical (experiential) learning is crucial. The hands-on aspect is particularly emphasized, encouraging students to learn by doing. This approach is essential for understanding and applying the course material in real-world scenarios, enabling students to effectively interact with data science teams within their organizations.

name: Management & Strategy
description:
This course provides students with a foundation about business organizations, management functions and strategy implementation.
The first section of the course will introduce concepts about the business organization, its operating environments, leadership, team building and management. 
The second half of the course will focus on the process of strategy development and implementation and performance management.

name: Capstone Project
description: The capstone project is a key component on the participant’s educational path on the Master in Innovation programme. Identification of the topic is to be made by the beginning of Term 2. Content can be built as the terms progress and students apply what they learn in modules and seminars. The capstone project is a Pass/Fail requirement of the Masters in Innovation programme, and the topic can be one of the following three broad categories with room for hybridization: a Design Project / Prototype; a Business Plan; or a Practical Innovation Study. The output of the work is a presentation at the end of Term 4, incl. a 10 to 25 page write-up (not including appendix) and the appendix/data package associated with the work.

name: Strategic Management in China
description: The primary topic of this course is strategic management in the Chinese context, including that of both local Chinese companies and foreign companies operating in China, but with a somewhat greater focus on the former. The course has two primary features. First, it broadly encompasses three levels of strategies of companies competing in the Chinese context: business strategies, corporate strategies, and cross-border competitive strategies. Second, in analyzing the strategies of companies competing in the Chinese context, the course will take a comparative perspective. The key frameworks in strategic management are mostly developed in the West. Since there are fundamental differences in macro national environment, competitive industry, and firm strategic issues between China and the West, whether the existing frameworks are applicable to the Chinese context is thus a key concern. We shall discuss throughout the course the similarities and differences between strategic management issues in the West and in China.

name: Internship
description: It is an intentional supervised learning related to one's field of study and career goals. Internships can be a very structured learning experience or they can be designed to meet the expectations of the student. Internships can be done locally or overseas. They can be part-time or full-time, paid or unpaid. Internships can be done during the academic year. The one thing all good internship opportunities have in common is they provide students with career-related work experience. Internship is done for a 20 week period.

name: Design Thinking for Innovation
description: This course introduces design thinking and its application to developing new products, services and the organization of businesses. Design thinking is a way of thinking and a structured set of techniques for creating innovations. Design thinking is a hot area which has the aim to help companies large and small (e.g. startups) to change and innovate. Design thinking as practiced in this course partly follows from the IDEO approach (see for example, www.ideo.com, but which also connects to other variants of design thinking. This blends creative thinking and logical or rational thinking, and involves a process consisting of the inspiration, ideation, and implementation sequence. It also involves underlying methods such as brainstorming, prototyping and systems thinking. Students will learn design methodologies and frameworks, and apply them through exercises and projects. The course is logically divided into five interconnected parts, but which we also separately emphasize. They are: (1) the design domains, including the artifacts to be designed (i.e., products, services, or the business itself), (2) the design methodologies (e.g. human-centered or ethnographic observation, brainstorming, the design process, systems thinking, design roles, team composition), and (3) the design contexts. Design contexts refers to the broader emerging context for designs and business, specifically, society (including different cultures and the poor), and the physical environment. Learning will be done primarily through case analyses, exercises, and a team project. Prototypes using paper or other easily accessed materials will be expected.

name: Innovation Strategy Developmen
description: This course introduces students to the theoretical concepts and analytical tools required for formulating and implementing appropriate strategies that affect the innovation success of the entire organization. Topics covered include external and internal environmental analyses, business-level strategies, corporate-level strategies, strategy process and implementation, innovation portfolio design and implementation and special topics such as competitive dynamics and competition in high tech industries. This course emphasizes the application of theory to the real world strategic issues. Students are encouraged to synthesize knowledge from other business courses into a comprehensive understanding of competitive advantage.

name: Innov-Focused Strat Leadership
description: This short module introduces students to core concepts in strategic management and how these translate to entrepreneurial ventures. Core concepts to be covered in strategic management include industry analysis, generic strategies and resource-based view through detailed case studies. How these core strategy concepts apply in the setting of new ventures involves careful consideration of potential retaliation from incumbents, how entrepreneurs should plan and recalibrate their product visions based on updated information over time. The focus on entrepreneurship touches on the motivation for entrepreneurs to develop new ventures, as well as stylized facts on new ventures.
