This course builds upon the foundational principles acquired in MKTG101 by providing a more in-depth understanding of how different marketing concepts fit together. It also aims to develop students’ ability to develop a strategic plan, beginning with an analysis of situation, the selection of the right target segments and the right competitive advantages, to the formulation of a coherent set of marketing actions that contribute to the company’s goals. A problem-solving approach is taken in the course, with the view that an effective solution to a marketing problem requires a thorough understanding of the consumer/market and of the competitive context.

This course is suitable not just for marketing majors, but anyone who has an understanding of basic marketing concepts and who wishes to have a good understanding of how strategic marketing can contribute to a company’s success.

name: Sales Management

school.name: Lee Kong Chian School of Business

description: This course is intended to introduce students to the role and importance of selling as a complement to marketing function in an organization. The two concepts are overlapping that one often says that “marketing needs selling” and “no selling can take place without marketing.” The instructor will guide students on how the sales function is operationalized in different kinds of marketing organizations as the scope can vary from consumer and retail marketing, trade marketing, services marketing, and business-to-business marketing. Students will cover this course under two parallel themes–the process of selling and the role of the professional sales team through the process of sales management. Students will learn the underlying body of marketing theory that underpins the study of sales management and personal selling. You will also learn some of the important principles of effective presentations related to sales proposals to organizational customers. A key delivery for this course would be for students to develop a case scenario to simulate a sales strategy involving target prospect calling, sales presentation and negotiations leading to sales conversion. The sales management course is focused on consumer trade marketing (pushing products through the channel) as well as business-to-business marketing applications for sales of business products and services to corporate customers.

name: Marketing Management

school.name: Lee Kong Chian School of Business

description: This course covers advanced topics in positioning and strategic market planning. This course draws on the rich body of literature in the field of marketing strategy and strategic market planning. The concepts, theories and ideas are given practical application in case histories and the dynamic marketing simulation COMPETE. Emphasis is placed on problem solving and use of analytical tools in the solution of marketing problems.

name: Marketing of Innovations

school.name: Lee Kong Chian School of Business

description: This course is designed to give students both appreciation and tools on how to utilise the twin growth engines of innovation and technology to create a high value business – profiting from innovations. Utilising innovative means, employing entrepreneurial marketing techniques, using technology as a lever and creating a small business-like environment are four key building blocks of this course. Utilising these four key areas can effectively generate significant high value for the business. Pre-requisite: MKTG101

name: Internet Marketing

school.name: Lee Kong Chian School of Business

description: This course is designed to equip students with the knowledge needed to make informed decisions concerning Internet strategy. From this course, students will learn about the various technologies driving the Internet, how they work, and how they will ultimately affect your decisions as an Internet marketing manager. This class will also cover several controversial, salient debates involving the Internet and related technologies that have the potential to affect us all.

name: Technology Marketing

school.name: Lee Kong Chian School of Business

description: This course focuses on the marketing of technology companies and their products or services. As I have often told past students in my marketing courses, get comfortable with ambiguity . Marketing success is rarely the result of a single inalterable, formulaic strategic plan. Instead, the best marketers understand that customers do not behave rationally and that even the best plans are constantly fine-tuned. Most importantly, great marketing provides a framework that creates a bias for action , not a bias for never-ending analysis and planning. Results only come when you actually try something, not think about trying something.

name: New Product Development

school.name: Lee Kong Chian School of Business

description: This course is designed to provide students with the intellectual foundation as well as experience of the new product development process. To develop intellectual foundations, students are expected to read the textbook, prepare for case studies, and participate in the class discussions. In addition, to get a real life experience of the new product development process, the students will work in groups for a semester long project. In the project they will identify a customer problem, propose a solution, test the solution and develop a plan for launching the product. At the end of the semester, the students can expect to have a richer understanding of the new product development process and be equipped with the state of the art tools and techniques that are essential for developing and launching new products.
graduateOutcomes: Understanding of global and Asian perspectives

name: B2B Marketing

school.name: Lee Kong Chian School of Business

description: The course will introduce students to business-to-business (B2B) Marketing. The course aims primarily to develop the student's ability to plan marketing activity in the B2B markets and in B2B2C supply chains. The structure of the course is to build upon basic Marketing Principles and reveal the interfaces of B2B marketing with other inter-firm business functions, especially channels, consultative sales, MarCom, and purchasing. We will examine the points of departure with consumer markets and take a more managerial approach. Key insights and concepts will be reinforced through Asian cases where possible from the SMU case collection. As B2B Marketing professionals in Singapore and the region know, a lot of B2B marketing here is regional or global. Keeping this in mind, we will bring an Asian and global perspective to the course.

name: Strategic Brand Management

school.name: Lee Kong Chian School of Business

description: Brand management is a vital component in the development and implementation of marketing strategy. This course helps students to better understand the process and techniques used by brand managers when leveraging their brands as the company’s strategic assets. This course is designed to develop students’ understanding of the importance of brand equity as well as how to build, measure and manage brand equity. Topics will include understanding brands from the customer’s perspective, building brand equity, measuring brand equity, leveraging the brand portfolios and managing brands over time and in different marketing context.
tracks: Marketing Major: Retail & Svc Mgmt Track
graduateOutcomes: Understanding of global and Asian perspectives

name: Financial Services Marketing

school.name: Lee Kong Chian School of Business

description: The course addresses the specific issues, from both a strategic and practical perspective, of marketing in the rapidly changing financial industry. The implications for financial marketing of increased competition, deregulation, compliance issues, a revolution in financial services related IT and globalisation will be examined and analysed. Customers, both corporate and individual are becoming more demanding of quality service and innovative products. These issues are examined in detail, particularly in terms of financial markets segmentation, product development, relationship management, brand development and distribution. In particular the course looks at the application of marketing concepts and principles and technology to develop customer insights and competitive intelligence in the financial market places of the Asia-Pacific region.

name: Marketing Chnls & New Retail

school.name: Lee Kong Chian School of Business

description: A significant domain of the study of marketing covers the roles of the Marketing Channels. It is the set of integrated business activities that must occur before products and services are made available to final consumers. This course will cover the concepts of channel functions comprising the supply side of designing routes to markets. The scope of this course covers both the business-to-business aspect of trade channel marketing as well as the business-to-consumer marketing now referred to as the “new retail.” The digital transformation of marketing is studied in relation to both its impact on channel marketing as well as consumer shopping behaviours. Marketing channels have recently been put into greater focus because of the challenges from the COVID-19 pandemic as well as the recent shocks on the supply chain created by political and economic uncertainties. The critical component of value creation for customers in marketing that is often overlooked is how customers want to buy. Therefore, the ability to make its products and services available to customers at the right place and time is a key source of creating customer value and competitive advantages for the marketing organization. Learning in this course will be supplemented through case studies of marketing channels in different product categories as well as industry expert talks.
tracks: Marketing Major: Retail & Svc Mgmt Track

name: Distribution Channel Mgmt

school.name: Lee Kong Chian School of Business

description:
Distribution channels bring the product or service available for consumption to customers at their convenient place of purchase.
The course shall build the foundation concepts of sales and channel management. This will be across spectrum of product categories, services and customers. At the same time, a connection of theory with real market place situations via cases and projects shall be established. The focus shall be on innovative thinking and discussions, while delivering the key concept messages. 
Channels Management shall provide framework for understanding channel design and structures, and its correlation to other components of marketing mix. The roles, functions and value additions of various channel types in ‘Go To Market’ ecosystem shall be analyzed. Variations across the product categories shall be examined.

name: Sports Marketing

school.name: Lee Kong Chian School of Business

description:
2007 will be a great year to study and learn about the business and marketing of sports.  From sports management to athlete endorsement to team ownership to corporate marketing campaigns, sports marketing has become a significant industry. 

This course will analyze the sports marketing business from strategy to planning to execution and evaluation. Several case studies will be used highlighting several regional and global sports.  Time does not allow for a review of all major international sports and related marketing, therefore, select sports and sports marketing examples from a regional and global perspective will serve as the foundation for the course.  The lessons, however, are useful across multiple sports and sports-related marketing.  More specifically, the course will examine sports marketing from several perspectives, including (but not limited to):

Strategy:
•	Brand development and management issues for leagues, teams, events, players
•	Product development at the league, team, event and player levels

Marketing and Implementation Mix:
•	Sponsorship 
•	Naming rights decisions for stadiums and similar sporting venues. 
•	Advertising and marketing communications 

International Perspectives:
•	Select sports: Olympics, World Cup, Regional and Global Sports
•	Trends 
•	Popularity
•	Fans 
•	Culture 

Challenges:
•	Decision making and evaluation for sports marketing activities

name: Customer Relationship Mgmt

school.name: Lee Kong Chian School of Business

description: Customer relationship management (CRM) is an important development within the field of marketing.  This course is designed to provide students with a good understanding of the concept of CRM.  To be successfully implemented, CRM should be viewed holistically.  Companies that had not done so had contributed to the high CRM failure rate we see today.  The aim of the course is to present a holistic view of CRM, covering its various perspectives including strategic, operational, analytical and collaborative.
tracks: Marketing Major: Retail & Svc Mgmt Track

name: Models for Mktg Dec Making

school.name: Lee Kong Chian School of Business

description:
Marketers today need to be equipped with knowledge and skills to make better marketing decisions. The purpose of this course is to equip participants with the knowledge and skills to use various tools to aid marketing decisions.  Participants will acquire critical skills that will allow them to model their customers’ behaviour, including choice modelling, satisfaction/loyalty modelling, price optimisation modelling and other types of quantitative modelling methods.
The course will be challenging, with students learning the concepts behind the various modelling methods and applying them on data provided by the instructor.  SPSS will be the primary software used in the course.  Other software that will be used include PERMAP (for perceptual mapping) and PLS (for structural equation modelling).  
Students are evaluated on individual assignments, group projects, class participation and term papers.

name: Int Mktg Comm: A Brand Persp
longName: Integrated Marketing Communications: A Brand Perspective

school.name: Lee Kong Chian School of Business

description: Marketing communications in the context of contemporary marketing has gone beyond the realm of the traditional tools of communications often classified as promotions. While advertising, public relations, sales promotions and personal selling remain the essence of the promotions mix, the intention of this course is to show how these tools are integrated not just within the promotions mix but also beyond the other elements of the marketing mix. The popular mantra applies here: “all elements of the marketing mix have the capacity to communicate.” Major changes primarily impacted by the use of the digital media as well as the global impact of messaging in marketing needs to be strongly factored in today’s study of marketing communications. Ultimately, the end outcome of IMC is its impact on the brand in terms of its ability to elevate brand awareness, brand recognition and ultimately brand preference and loyalty. In all aspects of the topics covered in this course, the focus would be on the connection between marketing communications and branding and how IMC can help organizations build long-term brand equity.
tracks: Marketing Major: Retail & Svc Mgmt Track

name: Marketing Analytics

school.name: Lee Kong Chian School of Business

description: The field of marketing is becoming increasingly data-oriented with firms building and growing their marketing analytics capabilities. This course provides you with the fundamental skills and tools to understand, process, analyze, and report marketing data and insights, all with the aim to improve marketing decision making. You will learn how to code in a programming language and how to use data visualization software. This is a hands-on course that will prepare you for jobs in marketing analytics, marketing technology, marketing intelligence, and data science.
areas: Grad Req - Dig Tech/Data Ana (Intake 2024 onwards)
Business Core-Dig Skls in Biz(Intake 2025 onwards)
tracks: Marketing Major: Retail & Svc Mgmt Track

name: Social Media and Content Mgmt

school.name: Lee Kong Chian School of Business

description:
One cannot deny the importance of social media. Social networking has become an integral part of the lives of most people. Through social media, we have become connected, not just with friends, but also with brands and businesses.

To Marketers, the world of social media has opened up a totally new communication arena for reaching out to current and potential customers. The opportunities to leverage on social media platforms to drive brands and businesses are tremendous. No longer do Marketers need to spend tons of advertising dollars to reach out to their audiences. Social media platforms seems like a godsend to the Brand and Marketing folks. But what exactly is Social Media Marketing? Is it as easy as it sounds? How can a brand market itself successfully on social media and what does it take?

In this course students will learn very practical social media marketing principles and the processes involved in marketing a brand on Social Media. Content is king when it comes to social media marketing and students will learn about content creation on social media to drive business objectives. Most importantly, students will have the opportunity to become social media marketers themselves. At the end of the course, they will have applied the principles they have learnt to a very exciting “real-life” project, which will give them a first-hand taste of what social media marketing in the business world is all about.

name: Mktg, Brandg & Svc Exc in Hosp
longName: Marketing, Branding and Service Excellence in Hospitality Industry

school.name: Lee Kong Chian School of Business

description:
This course helps students understand how a consumer-driven approach to marketing and branding is very important in the hospitality industry. There are hundreds of hospitality brands in the world, and new ones are being launched almost weekly.  As the industry grows ever more saturated, brands struggle to differentiate and innovate. Companies realize the importance of customer relationship management tools as well as continuously evolving communication channels like social media, mobile and review websites. However, companies strive to figure out which of the marketing channels to invest in to maximize their marketing dollars for profitability.

Through lectures involving examples, case studies, mini-experience assignments and a real group project with a partner company, students will be able to understand all aspects of hospitality marketing mix and branding. The course will address integrated marketing communication elements in-depth one by one through examples and/or guest speakers and explain 360 approach to branding. The course also includes visits to companies. For example, in the past we have visited Expedia and Facebook offices. 

The hospitality industry presents diverse career opportunities. This course will embed in you a consumer-driven brand management approach that you will be able to apply to any role within the hospitality industry.

Note that the course will be heavily focused on the hotel industry within the hospitality industry.

The course consists of overseas trips as part of the group project requirement. Please refer to the course outline for more details.

name: Marketing Channels

school.name: Lee Kong Chian School of Business

description:
Understanding marketing channels from a systems perspective is important in designing any go-to-market strategy. Marketing channels form the tentacles of an organization and provide immediate touch points to all stakeholders of an organization, for-profit, public or non-profit. Different marketing channels also have varying information-carrying capacities and, therefore, certain channels are more suited for specific kinds of communication. As such, having an in-depth knowledge of marketing channel systems and channel management is critical to marketing success. 

Designing channel structures within the macro marketing channel structure is a constraint firms face. Appreciating the tensions, pliability and rigidity of the macro marketing channel structure is essential to marketing channel design. Yet, marketing channel structures evolve. Effective management must understand how to capture opportunities and avoids being victims of rapidly evolving channel structures.

All marketing variables are important inhibitors as well as enhancers in channel member motivation. They form the basis of key considerations managing and mitigating channel conflicts. An immensely significant management task is coordinating the interaction of price as a key variable in market positioning and marketing channels as an organization’s external conduit of both physical and intangible flows.

Marketing channel design is a multi-disciplinary and multi-functional subjects to study and master. This course will be delivered through a combination of readings, class discussions, case analyses, video presentations, guest speakers, and a final marketing channel design project where you will work in a team to restructure channel strategies for an organization.

name: E-Commerce Marketing

school.name: Lee Kong Chian School of Business

description: This course teaches the principles and practices of e-commerce marketing, with emphasis on the skills needed to plan, launch, manage, market, and measure a Website that sells products and communicates with prospects and customers. Students will learn the specific processes that constitute core competencies for site development, including merchandising, pricing, and product display; best practices for maximizing click-through rate, stickiness, conversion of site visits to sales, as well as minimizing shopping-cart abandonment. They will also learn how to develop and manage the P&L and Operating Budgets for an e-commerce business and how to use the best practices of classic direct marketing and the latest technology in digital marketing to test, track and measure for Return on Investment and Customer Life Time Value. This course will provide students with a practical platform to understand, build and gain experience in sustaining successful e-commerce marketing initiatives. Students will learn all aspects of e-commerce marketing management. The course teaches them to employ a rigorous and holistic marketing methodology across both traditional and new-emerging techniques.

name: Sustainable Marketing

school.name: Lee Kong Chian School of Business

description: Much of marketing in the last half century has been about the single-minded satisfaction of consumer needs and wants. The key to success is thought to lie in thoroughly understanding what these needs and wants are and ensuring the best fit between what is offered as a product and what is desired. This market-led approach, unfortunately, is myopic in its neglect of other stakeholders, such as the environment and the community. This course takes an alternative perspective, premised on climate change, deterioration of the marine ecosystem, and social inequalities as realities. It first examines how current consumption patterns are harming the environment and communities. It then delves into what responsible consumption entails and how consumers can be influenced to make product choices that are sustainable. Theories in psychology will be drawn on to provide that understanding of consumer behaviour. The course will also examine what companies can do to ensure that their marketing activities are aligned with sustainability goals. Case studies of companies with strong sustainability initiatives will be used to illuminate current best practices.

name: Digital Advtising with Google

school.name: Lee Kong Chian School of Business

description:
Digital Advertising with Google is a partnership program with Google, which offers students with fundamental knowledge and skills in the digital marketing industry.  The advertising spending is estimated to be worth USD$768 million by the end of 2020 in Singapore, with an average annual growth rate of 6.5% since 2017. The industry will grow to USD$870 by 2023. It requires a lot of talents to take on various roles in the complex digital advertising ecosystem that can help companies optimize the results when using programmatic advertising.  

This course aims at offering students an overview of the programmatic advertising industry and introduce relevant concepts and skills to equip them for the industry. It will walk through the process of a programmatic ad buy, the ad-tech knowledge and skills-set required in programmatic buying, and how the advertisers can optimize their benefits.   

Upon the completion of the course, students will have the option of working as an intern at one of Google's partner companies or media agencies. Google will provide professional support to students throughout the learning journey.

Students who have taken Google’s Digitize Academy@SMU in 2019 should not bid for this course. The school will remove the student from the course if he/she has taken Google’s Digitize Academy@SMU in 2019.

name: Digital Marketing Strategy

school.name: Lee Kong Chian School of Business

description:
In the era of new digital technologies, the focus of marketing has shifted. It's no longer about selling a product or service but engaging with customers through relevant content and encouraging interactions that positively impact business. This advanced course recognizes this shift and is designed to equip students with a comprehensive understanding of digital marketing, incorporating established and emerging strategies.

This advanced course is delivered using an SMU-X learning approach. SMU-X is an experiential learning framework that calls for students to take on real-world challenges by collaborating on projects with corporations, non-profits, and government organizations. The framework represents a paradigm shift in the traditional teaching and learning approach, from teacher-centered to students taking ownership of their learning.

The course offers a comprehensive blend of theory, empirical analysis, and practical examples to reinforce key concepts related to digital marketing. Students will apply their knowledge to develop a digital marketing strategy for a real industry partner. We will collaborate with a real industry partner and offer consultancy services to recommend relevant digital marketing strategies for a real business problem.

With engaging seminars, case study discussions focusing on global brands, insights from industry experts with rich international business experience, and hands-on real business projects, students will sharpen their problem- solving skills to tackle real-world business problems through interdisciplinary approaches and activities. They are guaranteed an interactive learning experience that is informative and relevant to working for global businesses.

Do note that MKTG236 Digital Marketing Strategy follows the SMU-X experiential learning framework. It combines academic with experiential learning through the use of a project from an industry partner. Students need to take ownership of their learning. It is not designed to offer any software development training sessions and does not cover any IT programming. It is a contemporary marketing module to prepare students to join the marketing industry as a marketer.

name: Customer Acquisition

school.name: Lee Kong Chian School of Business

description:
Marketing is about customers.  Products come and go, but if you have a customer, you have a business.  So how do businesses attract customers?  How do they keep them?  

This course focuses on the new marketing tools and techniques—one-to-one marketing, databases, data mining and modeling, CRM, testing and measurement, and integrated marketing communications—that businesses use to attract the right new prospects, convert them to buyers, and gain their loyalty over the long term.  This kind of marketing is targeted, measurable and ROI-driven.  With these marketing approaches, marketing can be accountable to shareholders and stakeholders.

Strategies covered in this course include: data capture and data modeling, segmentation by customer value and behavior, buying process analysis, direct response communications, customer contact management, customer experience marketing, and marketing metrics and testing.  This course introduces the business, decision-making, strategic, tactical and operational skills essential to managing the customer asset.

name: EMarketing Strategy

school.name: Lee Kong Chian School of Business

description:
The Internet has taken the marketing world by storm.  This course will focus on the Internet as a tool for marketing communications, and as a sales channel (e-commerce), in both consumer and B-to-B markets.

Students will develop a familiarity with the elements of the Internet marketing toolkit, from email, RSS, and blogs, to search engine marketing, search engine optimization, banner advertising, rich media applications, affiliate marketing and behavioral targeting.  But each of these tools has its strengths and weaknesses.  Students will learn to evaluate the effectiveness of Internet marketing tools, and apply them to their best marketing use.  

The course will also train students on the principles of effective website design, both in terms of graphic appeal and for functionality and navigation.  Finally, this course will cover the tools and techniques of selling online, where e-commerce fits into an integrated selling program, and the functionality required in a successful e-commerce site.  Note: This course focuses on marketing, versus technology.

name: Pricing

school.name: Lee Kong Chian School of Business

description: This course aims to provide students with a roadmap to pricing strategically that would enable organizations to use pricing as a tool to drive profitability and sustainable growth. Students will learn new perspectives for determining product and service pricing to maximize a firm’s profits through creating and capturing customers.  This course provides insights into the strategies that managers can employ to determine the appropriate price to capture the value provided to customers. It addresses the major pricing decisions confronting managers in today’s competitive business environment by providing a comprehensive approach to managing pricing decisions.
tracks: Marketing Major: Retail & Svc Mgmt Track
graduateOutcomes: Understanding of global and Asian perspectives

name: Retail Strategy

school.name: Lee Kong Chian School of Business

description:
Retail Strategy is a considered as a retail capstone course in the marketing major as it builds on prior learning from the pre-requisite course of Retail Management. This course is an advanced and an applied subject in the domain of retail management and is intended to bridge the gap between academic learning and industry practice. In addition to retail management concepts learnt earlier, this course integrates learning from previous core subjects such as Consumer Behavior and Marketing Research as students will be expected to apply retail analytics in solving industry client-based problem challenges. This course will be built around assigned problem challenges given by retail organizations. This subject attempts to challenge senior year students’ abilities to research, test and recommend practical retail marketing and other related operational solutions to identify current gaps as well as to evaluate new retailing concepts and innovations. Students will be assessed by a combination of retail company problem challenges, new concept testing, consumer research, as well as case development.

Students will work in teams and will be expected undertake independent learning through client consultation, marketing research and site visits. They will be required to submit learning journals at periodic intervals to document the progress of their industry projects. In addition, they will be guided by updated readings which will require reflections on application of contemporary practices in retailing particularly in the digital context.
tracks: Marketing Major: Retail & Svc Mgmt Track

name: Business of Luxury

school.name: Lee Kong Chian School of Business

description: The goal of this course is to equip students with a profound understanding of the complexities of luxury marketing. Over the span of 13 weeks, students will delve into the unique dynamics that define the luxury business, exploring how luxury brand identity is crafted and maintained. They will gain insights into the psychology of luxury consumers, learning to harness these insights in brand management and product development. The course aims to foster a nuanced appreciation of brand communication, distribution and pricing strategies, alongside the integration of technology and sustainability considerations. By the end of the course, students will have demonstrated the ability to devise innovative and effective marketing strategies tailored to the luxury industry, blending theoretical knowledge with practical application.
graduateOutcomes: Understanding of global and Asian perspectives

name: Visual Design For Marketing

school.name: Lee Kong Chian School of Business

description:
Good design is essential in effectively delivering marketing messages. This course exposes students to key elements of good visual design in marketing. Students will learn the basic principles behind good graphic design, typography, colour theory and symbolism. Through a series of assignments, students will practice how to apply these principles towards composing influential and impactful marketing collaterals that deliver the intended message.

Students should be prepared for a heavier workload as the bulk of their learning will come from the practice and application of the design principles covered in class.

Please note that this is not a course on the Adobe creative suite, but rather, in using the tools to become a good marketer by learning how to translate their ideas to paper and communicate their ideas effectively.

name: MKTG WSE

school.name: Lee Kong Chian School of Business

description: The Marketing discipline is at the heart of achieving the goals of an organisation – large or small, in the private or public sector, in for-profit and non-profit organisations.  Understanding consumers, segmenting them into coherent groups, targeting segments based on their needs, designing a marketing strategy and executing specific tactics related to product design, branding, promotion, distribution and pricing are the defining functions of the Marketing discipline.  Consistently evaluating the effectiveness of the strategy in a competitive context, in the background of changes in the context (regulations, consumer trends, technological advances, supply setbacks and others) and meeting the needs of all stakeholders make Marketing a challenging profession.The Marketing Work-Study Elective (WSE) will be a collaboration with organisations from the public and private sectors to offer students an opportunity to undertake a 5-month (minimum) extended internship programme. With an extended internship timeframe, students will be able to immerse themselves in the functioning of the partner organisation, take on added responsibility, and experience the marketing profession as practiced in this firm.  Students will work on a specific project that is defined at the start of the term; over the course of the term, they may be assigned other work, but the focus of the WSE course will be one well defined project. The WSE will equip students with knowledge and skills that can be transferred to their future workplaces.The Marketing WSE involves an internship locally where students will work for at least four days each week at the partner organisation, and take courses on campus for up to one day each week. The internship will be for at least five months (e.g., August to December to cover Term 1, or January to May to cover Term 2).The WSE is open to all SMU students who meet the pre-requisites.

name: Marketing
description:
Marketing activity is the core of an operating business.   It provides the managerial focus for interfacing with customers and the source of intelligence about customers, competitors, and the general environment.  Managers must identify and measure consumers’ needs and wants, assess the competitive environment, select the most appropriate customer targets and then develop marketing programs that satisfy consumers’ needs better than the competition. Further, marketing focuses on the long-run relationship of a company to its customers as well as short- run sales and profits.
After three decades in which information technology (IT) was viewed by most senior executives as belonging solely to the “back office” of accounting and hum-drum transaction processing, IT has broken out. In many executive suites today, the talk now turns to the Internet, to electronic commerce, to knowledge management to network economy and to the issues involved in utilizing IT for “business transformation.” Understanding the new economy, which is at the interface of technology, economics and marketing is essential in successfully managing businesses in the future.
It is clear that, in an increasingly competitive global world, businesses must transform themselves to be more productive, to gather and store customer and competitive information and to capture the “tacit” knowledge that each employee holds in his/her head. Large software companies such as SAP, i2, and Oracle tout the potential to transform operations, supply chains, and customer relationships. A successful implementation of one of their software can provide new or better information to an organization’s decision makers, and enable global manufacturing and distribution processes. On the other hand, botched implementations can stymie product and service deliveries and prove extremely costly in at least the short term.
Firms are transforming their entire supply chain. At one end of the supply chain, companies like GE and major automobile manufacturers are demanding that all their suppliers interact with through the Internet. On the other end of the value chain, both Internet start-up companies and more established brick-and-mortar firms are enabling customers throughout the world to buy from them through the Internet. Increasingly, firms are enabling their customers to look into their internal systems to assess when orders will be delivered.
Industries themselves are rapidly changing form and business methods. The music industry, for example,  because  of  MP3,  (even  after)  Napster,  peer-to-peer  networks  (like  Gnutella, LimeWire) and Apple’s iPod and iTunes has undergone major transformation. More music is sold on-line than on CDs (Independent, may 12, 2012; http://www.independent.co.uk/arts- entertainment/music/news/more-music-downloads-sold-than-cds-7807443.html ). Amazon now sells more eBooks than printed books (BBC, August 6, 2012; http://www.bbc.co.uk/news/technology-19148146 ). New services have been created, some successful, such as on-line auctions (eBay, Ariba) and some not so successful such as grocery store delivery (Webvan). Partnerships and alliances are forming among former competitors, like competitors in technology services or transportation, in order to provide end-to-end services to large customers. New companies have emerged which have changed the way we communicate and share (Facebook, Twitter, YouTube, Instagram, Pinterest) and pay (PayPal, Square). Google has led the way to monetize search (96% of its $39 billion revenue now comes from online advertising; http://venturebeat.com/2012/01/29/google-advertising/ ).
One of the main objectives of this course is to provide you with an understanding of the strategic marketing issues faced by firms in the network economy, with special emphasis on how this has affected traditional and technology firms. This course should equip you with conceptual frameworks and analytical tools required to understand the new economy and manage fast paced traditional and technology businesses.
graduateOutcomes: Understanding of global and Asian perspectives

name: Marketing
description:
The course is designed to provide students with a deep understanding of the fundamental principies of marketing and marketing strategy making.

The focus will be on getting to know the basic techniques of defining and segmenting a target market for goods or services, building a brand with a meaningful positioning, and then integrating product, price, promotion and distribution to offer a superior marketing mix leading to a long-term competitive advantage.

Students  will be given an insight  into consumer  behavior  and brand management,  as well as understanding the role played by different marketing tools such as marketing research.

Both a theoretical and practical approach will be given in national and international markets so that the student will be able to deal with real situations.

The course objective is to provide students with an introduction to the fundamentals of marketing by introducing them to:

- The marketing concept
- A strategic marketing planning process
- Marketing analysis, including marketing research and consumer behaviour
- Market segmentation and brand positioning
- Product management, new product development and product life cycle.
- Pricing strategies.
- Brand building through integrated communications
- Leveraging distribution channels for competitive advantage
- New Marketing Trends

Additional objectives are:

- To introduce the student to the role of marketing in society.
- To expose the student to examples of how marketing has been applied.
- To improve presentation and writing skills and provide opportunities to articulate and defend positions.

The course has the dual purpose of introducing you to these concepts of marketing,  while also understanding how they fit together and operate in the real world. While a textbook provides more in- depth information about each of the components of marketing strategy, in the real world they operate together as an integrated plan and strategy. Case studies provide the experience of integrating the many aspects of marketing strategy analysis and planning. Thus, we use a textbook to give you a solid foundation and the cases to link your learning to the real world.

name: Dev Sales & Bus. Devt Success
longName: Developing Sales and Business Development Success
description:
The role of sales has evolved significantly in recent years. From mass marketing selling to complex business development activities, companies depend on having superior customer relationships to sustain growth, identify new opportunities and learn about competitor activities. Today’s sales professional operates like a mini-CEO: responsible for revenues, profits, distribution, pricing, customer identification, delivery, and support. At the corporate level, senior management has high expectations for its sales force, seeking top performances that achieve and exceed expectations. 

The course will provide:

1. A comprehensive examination of sales and business development activities and their role in company success
2. In-depth understanding of the buyer/seller relationship
3. An understanding of management’s role in sales and business development planning

name: Digital Media
description:
In less than 20 years, digital media and interactive services have transformed the way we live our daily lives.  Billions of people are connected across the world through the use of the internet and mobile phones; the amount of content, information, and entertainment that is available to the average “connected” individual is endless; and the average “connected” teen consumes more media than ever before. 

While consumers have led the adoption of interactive services and digital media, many companies find themselves reacting to consumer demand. Occasionally, the reaction of companies to consumer demand is sufficiently addressed and timed.  Often times however, companies are either late or unequipped to deliver on their consumers digital needs.  In many developed countries, newspaper and print publication companies find themselves in a very difficult situation as many of them have failed to adapt to the changing consumer demand.

This course will explore issues related to digital media and interactive services.  It will cover topics such as: predominant digital business models, strategies of the major digital players, consumer behavior, the impact on digital marketing, differences between developed markets and developing markets, and product development practices in digital companies.  Special emphasis will be placed on discussing tools for the marketer in the digital age. 

This course will be relevant for those who have an interest in the internet, technology, media, or telecommunication sectors as well as those who would like to explore best practices around digital marketing.

name: Strategic Brand Management
description: As the world’s economic centre of gravity continues to shift eastward, more global brands are to emerge from Asia. You and the companies you will likely be working are not only to witness these developments from nearby, you are also in a great position to shape the future brand landscape. To have impact on the creation of strong future brands in an increasingly global, dynamic, innovation-disruptive and connected marketplace, it is necessary to strategically manage these valuable market-based assets. Imperative is to develop processes and procedures for successful brand strategies. This course will address the strategic brand management processes: brand creation, development and maintenance. Still, these key processes can never bring the brand entirely under the firm’s control: it is the customer who owns the brand. How to then manage such a competitive asset? The course will, therefore, go beyond just providing branding knowledge. It will create a co-creation space in which participants can experiment with branding practices.

name: Emerging Markets Management
description:
This course will examine the entrepreneurial forces driving the high-tech growth in China and India. The students will learn the strategic issues, making key marketing decisions, develop a strategy and design and organizational structure while entering a new market.

Class discussions will focus on many interesting case studies like Microsoft in China & India, Lenovo's Dell challenge, Motorola & Cisco in China, \"Intel Inside\", GE's Talent machine, IBM's \"On Demand Business\" in India, etc.

Finally, the students will develop strategies to enter Vietnam and India for PC & Cell OEM's and present them in the class.

name: Strategic Marketing
description:
This course provides a unique practitioner’s perspective on the strategic marketing process. This mini elective will introduce the “end to end” strategic marketing process, illustrate the key elements involved at each step and share the best practices from some of the leading companies.  While conceptual frameworks will be presented, the focus of this program will be to bring in practical and real-life experiences and learning from various industries.   

The course will cover:
1.	Understanding of the overall strategic marketing process and each step involved
2.	Best practices on segmentation and value proposition development
3.	Ways to define a unique competitive positioning and build a strong brand
4.	Approaches on pricing strategy and profitability management
5.	Developing a robust marketing and sales plan

name: Consumer Behaviour
longName: Consumer Behaviour: Theory, Research Methods and Applications
description:
Consumer Behaviour (CB) is the inter-disciplinary science of understanding the impact of marketing actions on consumers. This course has been specially designed to convey the essence of the most important CB theories (from individual level to macro level), the most essential research techniques, and applications of both theories and research techniques to diagnosing marketing problems and arriving at solutions. This course will help you improve your ability to anticipate consumer reactions, to predict their responses and most importantly, to measure the ultimate impact on consumers.  It is intended to help students who wish to work in consulting or in branding/marketing/advertising in B2C firms.

The course will provide:
1.	An introduction to consumer behaviour theory on the effects of marketing on consumer awareness, perceptions, memory, attitudes and decision-making
2.	A managerial guide to using the research techniques of systematic observation, qualitative research, surveys and experiments
3.	A framework to use these theories and techniques in diagnosing and researching the most typical marketing decisions in B2C firms

name: Customer Relationship Mgmt
description:
Customer relationship management (CRM) is an important development within the field of marketing.  If understood and implemented well, CRM can give a company a significant competitive edge.  This course is designed to help managers gain a good understanding of CRM concepts and to effectively put CRM into practice.  For CRM to be effective, it must be holistically implemented within the organization.  The high rate of CRM failures in companies today suggest that this requirement is not met.  The aim of the course is to present a holistic view of CRM, covering its various perspectives including strategic, operational, analytical and collaborative.

The course will provide:

1.	An in-depth understanding of the concepts of CRM and its role in giving companies a competitive edge
2.	A comprehensive understanding of CRM analytical tools necessary for designing sound CRM strategies 
3.	A practical guide for CRM implementation within an organisation
4.	An understanding of organisational considerations necessary for successful CRM implementation

name: Strategic Marketing Management
description: This course provides senior executives an understanding of the important function that Strategic Marketing plays in the long term performance of the firm. This module addresses the key challenges associated with aligning marketing activities with corporate strategy. It will provide frameworks, concepts, and tools necessary to ensure that marketing organizations are focused on the appropriate and measurable activities that drive business results and their marketing functions are staffed with and led by the right people.  In addition, the module explores the strategic opportunities and vulnerabilities associated with the management of customer relationships.  This is achieved by exploring approaches to building customer loyalty and developing effective systems to manage and maintain customer relationships.
graduateOutcomes: Understanding of global and Asian perspectives

name: Biz to Biz Distribution Mgmt
description:
Marketing Channels and Business to Business Management is one of the most exciting, challenging topics in marketing.  An ability to organize an effective marketing channels and distribution is often between success and failure in the marketplace.  Indeed, marketing channels and distribution is a key strategic asset that can lead to sustainable competitive advantages.  

This course will provide the students the knowledge of planning marketing channel activities, organizing institutions and agencies involved in the process of making products and services available to business and household consumers, coordinating the marketing efforts of those institutions and agencies, evaluating the performance of those organizations, and controlling marketing channel efforts.

name: Dist Chn, Brand Bldg & Int P P
longName: Distribution Channels, Brand Building and Intellectual Property Protection
description:
Marketing Channels and Distribution Management is one of the most exciting, challenging topics in marketing.  An ability to organize an effective marketing channels and distribution is often between success and failure in the marketplace.  Indeed, marketing channels and distribution are a key strategic asset that can lead to sustainable competitive advantages.  

This course will provide the students the knowledge of planning marketing channel activities, organizing institutions and agencies involved in the process of making products and services available to business and household consumers, coordinating the marketing efforts of those institutions and agencies, evaluating the performance of those organizations, and controlling marketing channel efforts. 

All the while, this course will look at the brand building aspects of the channel and the opportunity for protecting and enhancing brand strength.

name: Marketing Research Appln
description: Marketing is increasingly challenging in a world of the “connected consumer”. And the role of marketing research has also changed to keep pace – from data collection to data integration and analysis. But as the cliché goes “garbage in – garbage out”, it is fundamental to have a strong grounding in understanding information needs before we move to integration and analysis. This course will prepare the students to scope marketing information needs that are crucial to making informed decisions using marketing research. After this course, students will be able to provide a better brief to marketing research agencies and understand and appreciate the applications of marketing research.

name: Crafting & Providing Services
description:
Services industries constitute for a majority of the 2013 GDP of countries like Singapore (65%), Brazil (69%), Russia (60%), India (57%), and United States (79%)1. Not surprisingly, over the last decade, many traditional “goods” manufacturers such as IBM, General Electric, HP, and Dell have turned to offering services to their clients with the objective of becoming “solution” providers with differentiated and higher margin offerings. In fact, many reports from consulting firms such as McKinsey, Booze Allen & Hamilton, suggest that as the world of business transforms into a global knowledge economy, value creation for customers is primarily going to shape through provision of services, rather than goods.

Despite these assertions, the business press is replete with stories of how Service Quality is either declining or varies widely across firms, and how it is very difficult for firms to consistently offer good Service Quality. Indeed, the American Customer Satisfaction Index consistently reports lower levels of customer satisfaction of consumers for firms offering services as compared to goods.2 Against, this background, this course is designed for MBA students seeking to develop a deeper understanding of services. The specific objectives of the course are: (i) to develop an understanding and appreciation of the key theoretical concepts and tools in the domain of services, and (ii) to enhance the decision making skills related to multiple facets of marketing services.

name: Defining & Creating New Market
description: This course provides the student with the managerial insights to perceive opportunity in markets that currently may not exist, or where current solutions apply to other markets. Both the positioning and strategy issues, and marketing activities of the innovative business are explored. This course allows students who wish to learn how to develop and execute marketing strategies in intensive, fast changing markets, including those characterised by shrinking product life cycles and rapid turnover in the knowledge and information. The course pushes students to consider future opportunities in new spaces.

name: Data Model & Mktg Dec Making
description:
Decision making is an essential skill for managers.  With multivariate analytical modeling techniques available and good software support, managers today with access to data are able to use that to make better management decisions.  Participants will acquire critical skills that will allow them to model the behavior of customers, employees, and the market in which the company competes.  Examples of modeling applications include employee engagement modeling, customer satisfaction/loyalty modeling, and market brand perception.  The skill acquired will enable participants to identify management problems that can be modeled and subsequently apply the techniques to make decisions.

Students learn the concepts behind the various modeling methods and apply them in management scenarios with data supplied by the instructor.  SPSS will be the primary software used in the course.

name: Integrating Strategy with Exec
description:
The Big Picture is an integrated Framework that helps marketers transform the way they analyze and solve the challenges and opportunities they face in their business. 

The framework takes the form of a funnel, where each successive set of decisions brings increased focus to the strategy development and implementation planning process. These four steps help the student in answering four critical questions:

1. What is the firm’s overall business objective?
2. What are the primary tenets of the firms’ strategy?
3. What is the firm’s executional plan?
4. How will the firm analyze and integrate results?

name: Digital Marketing Strategy
description:
Total advertising spend worldwide will reach $518 billion (Financial Times, June 5, 2013, ZenithOptimedia). Online advertising spend will over $113 billion of which $37 billion will be spent in Asia Pacific (Group M, March 2013). 47% of the marketers in the US said that they will be shifting 20-30% of their traditional marketing spend to digital. Social network ad spend will reach $11 billion in 2014, 62% of it will be spent on Facebook (eMarketer, November 2012). 

This new media presents many challenges to marketing professionals. Where once much of the ad spend devoted to traditional media was typically one way (i.e. from the firm to the consumer), the explosion of social media demands a two way conversation. The increasing use of user generated content and the platforms that facilitate their influence means that the firm does not have control on what messages are being circulated about the firm and its brands. Understanding the digital technologies, the social media tools and the mechanisms by which consumers get influenced is important in developing future marketing communication strategies. This course provides frameworks to understand the new digital marketing landscape and mechanisms on how firms can effectively develop their digital marketing strategies.

name: Marketing
description: To maintain or enhance their competitiveness, companies aim to identify market opportunities and challenges and respond accordingly. Marketing plays a vital hinge role between the external environment of a firm, i.e., the market, consumers, and competitors, and the internal capabilities and resources of the firm. The module structure is designed based on the marketing’s aim to support firm value creation. It comprises the following main areas. We are going to devote the first session to what marketing is, how it has evolved over time, and how it relates to markets (external environment) and corporate strategy (internal environment). Next, to develop and implement an effective marketing strategy, companies require a clear understanding of the market and consumer behavior, which can be gained through insights from market research (sessions 2 & 3). Based on such market knowledge, companies can design offerings, i.e., value propositions that have the potential to create superior customer value (session 4). The next step is to communicate the value proposition (sessions 5-6), which involves selecting the best communication instruments. Next, to deliver value, the firm needs to choose the most suitable sales channel and manage the sales process effectively. For services in particular, the process, staff, and physical facilities are also part of the marketing mix instruments (session 7). These are value-creating activities within the marketing mix. To capture the value that has been created, it is essential to understand how to determine an appropriate price or pricing model (week 8). These so-called Marketing Mix instruments taken together constitute the scope of the brand. In week 9, we will discuss what brands are, how firms create their brand architectures, and how to decide about brand extensions. In week 10, we will focus on how firms create value over time. Specifically, we will discuss relationship marketing and loyalty programs. Throughout the module, we will examine how firms monitor value creation using marketing metrics. The latter is important since marketing is increasingly under scrutiny to prove that activities generate a return on investment.
graduateOutcomes: Understanding of global and Asian perspectives

name: Understanding Mkt & Dev Biz Mo
longName: Understanding Markets and Developing Business Models
description: This module covers the basics of effective go-to-market strategies and sales management efforts in the context of an organization’s ecosystem and collaborative ties with customers, suppliers, distributors, sales force etc. It is aimed at enabling students to perceive and create opportunities in markets that currently may not exist (or where current solutions may apply to other markets) and to appreciate effective positioning and strategic marketing issues/activities (incl. strategic pricing) with regard to innovative business models in an era of fast changing markets and shrinking product life cycles. Another key goal of the course unit is to ensure that students know how to create a greater market share for the respective innovation through successful market education, effective launch management tactics, brand leadership and value selling.

name: Managing Service Innovations
description: This course introduces students to the basic conceptual frameworks and tools for crafting and delivering innovative service offerings to both b2b and b2c customers. To achieve these objectives, the students will be expected to carefully go through the assigned readings to understand the basics of management of service-based offerings. The course will be taught in the form of lectures and in-depth case study discussions.

name: Seminar
description:
Pricing Strategy

The class will cover the following key pricing strategy decisions that managers have to make to set prices. 
1. Value Pricing
2. Segmented pricing
3. Dynamic pricing
4. Managing Price Competition 
5. Building pricing capability

The pricing strategy topics will be covered using cases, lectures, interactive class exercises and assignments.

Marketing Analytics

Most MBA students who go into management consulting or marketing positions will find themselves having to advise their firm on critical aspects related to product management, understanding customer behavior, and improving the performance of a product in the market. This course systematically covers the various stages of analytics used in a marketing firm. We will study several essential data-driven analytical methods; we will implement these methods using state-of-the art software, and solve real problems using real data. This course is very hands-on and will have components of lectures and in-class discussions and practice sessions.

The course aims to train students to determine answers to the following basic questions that MBAs encounter in their jobs when trying to improve the sales position of their product.

• What decision factors do customers use in deciding whether they should buy my product or my competitors' products? How can I influence the decision factors that customer’s use?
• What segments of customers would like my product? Which customer segments should I try to attract?
• How should the improved product version be introduced in the context of my existing product portfolio?
• How should I implement advertising? How do I select creative? What is the appropriate media mix?
• How do I ensure effective distribution? How should I select and choose retail locations and sales force presence?

name: Seminar
description: Students are to refer to the seminar details provided

name: Applied Mktg Res. & Analytics
description:
Business managers utilize marketing data to assess the return on their investments and better understand their customers. Analyzing large marketing datasets also allows managers to recognize and justify their marketing mix decisions. This course is designed to meet the increasing needs of industry and recruiters in applying quantitative and analytical skills for advanced marketing decision-making. The content of this course is based on cutting-edge research in both academic and practitioner communities. The course provides students with an opportunity to analyze real-world marketing problems. 

The best way to learn all the material in this course is through “hands-on” experience. As such, we will use recent developments in statistical science to examine solutions to important issues faced in marketing research. There will be various datasets and tools provided and used in the class to get practical experience about Marketing Analytics. Specifically, we will discuss market and segmentation techniques, regression and choice modeling, economic models of pricing, advertising and optimization techniques. The emphasis being on understanding, interpretation and proper use of marketing research techniques. One of the goals of this course is to train knowledgeable marketing managers who can evaluate the quality of marketing research and utilize the information to effectively make strategic decisions. The primary aim of this course is to learn new skills and tools that will provide students with important quantitative acumen for success in a marketing career.

name: Technology Enabled Business
description:
As businesses move away from brick and motor and create new business models that are heavily reliant on technology. This course aims to provide students with the necessary skills to see how the world of business is changing and what are the critical elements of a technology enabled business. 

The course would cover aspects relating to business models, financial aspects, supply chain management and technology leverage for management as well as consumer insights.  The course would entail discussion around business strategies and financial models for e-commerce for risk management, the applications of consumer analytics to e-commerce, and the operational challenges and innovations in e-commerce fulfilment.

The course would be an eight week elective, each aspect covered over two weeks. The course would be offered across all the PGPP programs.

name: Marketing Analytics
description:
This course is designed to meet the increasing needs of industry and recruiters in applying quantitative and analytical skills for understanding consumer decision-making. Business managers utilize marketing data to assess the return on their investments and better understand their customers. The course provides students with an opportunity to analyse real-world marketing problems. 
The best way to learn all the material in this course is through “hands-on” experience. As such, we will use developments in statistical science to examine solutions to important issues faced in consumer analytics. There will be various datasets and tools provided and used in the class to get practical experience. Specifically, we will discuss market and customer segmentation techniques, regression and choice modelling, economic models of pricing, retail and web analytics. The emphasis being on understanding, interpreting and proper use of these research techniques. The primary aim of this course is to learn new skills and tools that will provide students with important quantitative acumen for understanding consumer analytics.

name: Consumer Behaviour
description:
Virtually all decisions involved in developing an effective marketing mix for a product or service rely on in-depth knowledge of the consumers who comprise the target market. The success of many companies and non-profit organizations—whether they be Coca-Cola, Procter & Gamble, Apple, or TWG Tea—lies in genuine insights into the minds, hearts, and behaviors of their target consumers. Thus, a clear understanding of the principles, concepts, and results of consumer behavior is critical to success in marketing. However, while all of us are
ourselves consumers, our intuitions about our own behavior as well as that of other consumers are unfortunately often inaccurate. This over-reliance on our own intuition has led managers astray, resulting in poor managerial
decision making for their organizations.

The purpose of this course is to help students gain insights into the principles and processes of consumer behavior. In doing so, students will be able to use their understanding of consumer behavior to evaluate and develop effective marketing strategies. To achieve these learning objectives, in this course we will directly
examine extant theory and research concerning the behavior of the consumer, with the goal of understanding how marketing managers can use these ideas to design their marketing programs. Knowledge of consumer behavior requires an understanding of important theoretical concepts from related fields such as psychology, sociology, economics, etc. Given the nature of the subject, while marketing applications will be discussed throughout the course, this course will be heavier on theory compared to other marketing courses.

name: Marketing
description:
Marketing activity is the core of an operating business.   It provides the managerial focus for interfacing with customers and the source of intelligence about customers, competitors, and the general environment.  Managers must identify and measure consumers’ needs and wants, assess the competitive environment, select the most appropriate customer targets and then develop marketing programs that satisfy consumers’ needs better than the competition. Further, marketing focuses on the long-run relationship of a company to its customers as well as short- run sales and profits.
After three decades in which information technology (IT) was viewed by most senior executives as belonging solely to the “back office” of accounting and hum-drum transaction processing, IT has broken out. In many executive suites today, the talk now turns to the Internet, to electronic commerce, to knowledge management to network economy and to the issues involved in utilizing IT for “business transformation.” Understanding the new economy, which is at the interface of technology, economics and marketing is essential in successfully managing businesses in the future.
It is clear that, in an increasingly competitive global world, businesses must transform themselves to be more productive, to gather and store customer and competitive information and to capture the “tacit” knowledge that each employee holds in his/her head. Large software companies such as SAP, i2, and Oracle tout the potential to transform operations, supply chains, and customer relationships. A successful implementation of one of their software can provide new or better information to an organization’s decision makers, and enable global manufacturing and distribution processes. On the other hand, botched implementations can stymie product and service deliveries and prove extremely costly in at least the short term.
Firms are transforming their entire supply chain. At one end of the supply chain, companies like GE and major automobile manufacturers are demanding that all their suppliers interact with through the Internet. On the other end of the value chain, both Internet start-up companies and more established brick-and-mortar firms are enabling customers throughout the world to buy from them through the Internet. Increasingly, firms are enabling their customers to look into their internal systems to assess when orders will be delivered.
Industries themselves are rapidly changing form and business methods. The music industry, for example,  because  of  MP3,  (even  after)  Napster,  peer-to-peer  networks  (like  Gnutella, LimeWire) and Apple’s iPod and iTunes has undergone major transformation. More music is sold on-line than on CDs (Independent, may 12, 2012; http://www.independent.co.uk/arts- entertainment/music/news/more-music-downloads-sold-than-cds-7807443.html ). Amazon now sells more eBooks than printed books (BBC, August 6, 2012; http://www.bbc.co.uk/news/technology-19148146 ). New services have been created, some successful, such as on-line auctions (eBay, Ariba) and some not so successful such as grocery store delivery (Webvan). Partnerships and alliances are forming among former competitors, like competitors in technology services or transportation, in order to provide end-to-end services to large customers. New companies have emerged which have changed the way we communicate and share (Facebook, Twitter, YouTube, Instagram, Pinterest) and pay (PayPal, Square). Google has led the way to monetize search (96% of its $39 billion revenue now comes from online advertising; http://venturebeat.com/2012/01/29/google-advertising/ ).
One of the main objectives of this course is to provide you with an understanding of the strategic marketing issues faced by firms in the network economy, with special emphasis on how this has affected traditional and technology firms. This course should equip you with conceptual frameworks and analytical tools required to understand the new economy and manage fast paced traditional and technology businesses.

name: Integrated Marketing Comm
description:
With the digital revolution, advertising is wrongly losing its lustre. Long-term, sustained business growth cannot come by targeting loyal users, or by running short-term promotions, or by prioritizing e-commerce over everything. To grow brands need to target all consumers, including – or especially – light users of the brand. With the proliferation of brands that essentially deliver similar benefits and the increasingly crowded lifestyle of consumers, who have a million things vying for their attention, the marketer’s task today is particularly challenging. They need to help their brand make an emotional connection with the consumer and thereby become ‘mentally available’. The key to this is powerful advertising. 

However advertising can no longer rely on traditional television-skewed media. And it can no longer be only one-way communication from the brand to the consumer. Today advertising needs to be delivered in an increasingly digital manner to an increasingly hyper-active, digitally-connected consumer. 

The course covers two key areas:
1. It teaches a systematic approach to develop powerful advertising, as described above, focusing particularly on writing the communications strategy, developing a clear, focused creative brief (which should include a meaningful consumer insight) and using a practical framework to evaluate ideas from the ad agency. 

2. Once the advertising campaign is ready, the course teaches the principles of planning its execution in a holistic, integrated way across the right media, both digital and conventional. 

The course targets marketing professionals and is designed to help students embarking on a career in marketing (primarily as client but also as agency executive).  It is based on the content of my book, Spark: How Powerful Insights and Brilliant Advertising Can Grow Brands, soon to be published by Simon & Schuster.

name: Digital Marketing
description: The aim of this course is to prepare students for real world challenges in digital marketing.   This course will equip students with the essential knowledge, concepts and frameworks to analyse specific marketing issues, develop an integrated digital marketing strategy, monitor and measure its results.   It covers various digital marketing tools and online platforms used to formulate and implement digital marketing strategies.  Topics covered include digital transformation, new marketing normal, online presence, social platform, content marketing, social media marketing, paid social promotion, search engine optimization, paid search, lead nurturing and lead conversion, and online performance management.   Students will learn from an experiential learning approach which prepares them to make effective marketing decisions.

name: V. Selling as Driver of Biz G
longName: Value Selling as A Driver of Business Growth
description: This module covers the basics of effective (value) sales management efforts in the context of an organization’s ecosystem and collaborative ties with customers, suppliers, distributors, sales force etc. It is aimed at enabling students to identify and create sales opportunities in markets that currently may not exist (or where current solutions may apply to other markets) and to appreciate what it takes to create customer value through the application of value-based selling techniques as driver of business growth in an era of fast changing markets and shrinking product life cycles. Another key goal of the course unit is to ensure that students know how to influence prospects practically so that customer interests and concerns are effectively served and the deal is successfully sealed.

name: Advanced Marketing Strategy
description:
This course will take the CEO’s perspective on marketing. Specifically, to build the marketing capabilities in you to address the marketing challenges topmost in the minds of CEOs today in the face of changing market place realities.  

The course will be based on the premise that marketing as a discipline has failed CEOs and companies. If marketing is to be effective in meeting the CEO and Board level challenges, then marketing has to become:

• more strategic, more cross-functional, and more bottom-line oriented
• effective in the face of new competitors like retailers, low cost rivals, and emerging giants
• help the transition to new channels and new media

Our focus will be on the business unit and its network of suppliers, channels, customer relationships, and alliances. Taking the viewpoint of the CEO and the general manager, the course will focus on three over-riding themes: 

- Successful marketing strategies deliver superior customer value; 
- Successful implementation of these strategies requires orchestrating the entire value network and marketing mix in an effective and consistent manner; and 
- Marketing innovation can be used as a driver for changing the existing rules of the game in an industry.
graduateOutcomes: Understanding of global and Asian perspectives

name: Marketing Management
description: The course will offer an introduction to marketing as a mindset, as a capability, and as techniques to reach the consumer. It will be assumed that the student has no formal training in the marketing discipline. While, it is not intended to go into depth on any of the subjects and areas of marketing that will be explored, the student should get a thorough introduction to what is marketing, how marketers think, and what are the various components of effective marketing, The electives are the place where students go deep into understanding marketing areas such as pricing, promotion, digital marketing and social media, big data, salesforce, omni-channel distribution, and branding.
